records.title: Heart Failure
records.intro: Heart failure is a condition in which the heart cannot supply as much blood as the body needs. With appropriate treatment and management, it is possible to maintain daily life, but if left untreated, symptoms such as shortness of breath and swelling can worsen. If you have risk factors such as high blood pressure, diabetes mellitus, or obesity, please see a medical specialist regularly.
records.tags_raw: heart failure, dyspnea, edema, heart, obesity, high blood pressure, myocardial infarction, heart medication, heart failure prevention, breathlessness, difficulty breathing, labored breathing, feeling of suffocation, body swelling, facial swelling, leg swelling, swelling in hands and feet

sections.heading: Definition
sections.content:
Heart failure is a condition in which, because of a structural or functional abnormality of the heart, the body's organs do not receive as much oxygen (blood) as they need.



· Structural abnormality: a problem in the coronary arteries (the blood vessels that supply the heart), the myocardium (the heart muscle), the valves (the "doors" inside the heart), the pericardium (the membrane surrounding the heart), and so on.

· Functional abnormality: a problem with the heart's ability to contract or relax, or an accompanying arrhythmia (an irregular heartbeat).



With good treatment, it is possible to carry on with daily life without major problems while continuing medication and outpatient visits. In recent years, people with risk factors such as high blood pressure, diabetes mellitus, and obesity have also been regarded as being at risk for heart failure and managed in advance.

sections.heading: Causes
sections.content:
The causes of heart failure can be divided broadly into two groups.



■ Cardiovascular Causes

· Ischemic heart disease: such as myocardial infarction (a condition in which a blocked heart vessel damages the heart muscle)

· High blood pressure

· Valve disease

· Buildup of substances such as amyloid in the heart muscle

· Reduced heart function caused by alcohol, anticancer drugs, or toxins

· Tachycardia (an abnormally fast heart rate)



■ Systemic Diseases and Conditions

· Excessive stress

· Hyperthyroidism (a condition in which too much thyroid hormone is produced)

· Myocarditis (inflammation of the heart muscle)

· Rheumatic diseases



Heart failure can also occur without any underlying disease, for example after intake of certain substances, cancer treatment, or myocarditis following a cold.

sections.heading: Symptoms and Diagnosis
sections.content:
■ Main Symptoms

The typical symptoms of heart failure are shortness of breath and edema (swelling of the body). These symptoms can also be caused by other conditions, such as lung disease and kidney disease, so an accurate diagnosis is needed. If you have any unusual symptoms, please consult a medical specialist.



■ Diagnostic Process

Diagnosis proceeds in the following order:

1. Medical history and physical examination: symptoms and past medical history are reviewed.

2. Basic tests: blood tests, chest X-ray, electrocardiogram (a test of the heart's electrical signals), and echocardiography (a test that checks the structure and function of the heart) are performed. These are used to confirm heart failure, to distinguish it from other conditions, and to decide on medication.

3. Additional tests: depending on the suspected cause, CT, angiography (a test that looks at the condition of the blood vessels), MRI, and others may also be performed.

sections.heading: Treatment and Medication
sections.content:
When heart failure is diagnosed, medication is started along with treatment of the underlying cause. After treatment, heart function may improve or symptoms may get better.



■ The Importance of Continuing Medication

Heart failure medications are used in combination to prevent the heart's function from worsening in several different ways. If medication is stopped after heart function has recovered, there is a risk that it will worsen again. One study reported that heart function declined again in 44% of patients who stopped their medication after recovery, with the decline reported to begin especially from 8 weeks after stopping medication.

Medication can be adjusted depending on blood pressure or symptoms, but stopping it completely on your own carries a high risk of worsening heart failure. Please be sure to consult your treating physician to adjust your medication.

sections.heading: Prevention and Frequently Asked Questions
sections.content:
■ Relationship Between Obesity and Heart Failure

Obesity is closely linked to risk factors for heart failure such as high blood pressure and diabetes mellitus. Studies have found that obesity alone, even without metabolic syndrome (a combination of conditions such as high blood pressure, diabetes mellitus, and hyperlipidemia), raises the risk of heart failure compared with normal weight. Heart failure can occur in people with obesity even at a young age, in their 20s and 30s, and even without a family history.



■ Does Eating Salty Food Raise the Risk of Heart Failure?

A habit of eating salty food is a major cause of high blood pressure and is also a risk factor for coronary artery disease and stroke. One study reported that, even after adjusting for other factors, the group with higher salt intake had a higher risk of heart failure. It is advisable to keep a habit of eating low-salt food.



■ Lifestyle Habits for Prevention

· Weight management through an appropriate diet and exercise

· A low-salt diet

· Early detection and management of risk factors through regular health checkups

If you have any unusual symptoms or risk factors, please consult a medical specialist.

records.title: Deep Vein Thrombosis (DVT)
records.intro: Deep vein thrombosis is a condition in which a blood clot (a lump formed when blood coagulates) develops in a deep vein of the leg and blocks the vessel. Leg swelling and pain are the main symptoms, and if the clot travels to the lungs, a dangerous complication called pulmonary embolism can occur. If you suspect symptoms, please consult a medical specialist right away.
records.tags_raw: deep vein thrombosis, DVT, blood clot, pulmonary embolism, leg swelling, economy class syndrome, dry cough, persistent cough, cough that won't stop

sections.heading: Definition and Causes
sections.content:
Deep vein thrombosis is a condition in which a blood clot forms in a deep vein inside the leg muscles and blocks the vessel. Veins carry blood from the legs back to the heart, and during this process the leg muscles contract and push the blood upward. However, if you sit or lie in the same position for a long time, the leg muscles do not move, blood pools, and a clot can form.



■ Major Risk Factors

· Sitting for long periods (long-haul flights, long hours at a computer, etc.)

· Staying in bed for a long time after surgery or injury

· Cancer patients, pregnancy, and obesity

· A previous episode of deep vein thrombosis

· Blood clotting disorders

sections.heading: Symptoms
sections.content:
The following symptoms may occur:

· Swelling that is noticeably worse in one leg

· Leg pain or tenderness (pain when pressed)

· Reddened skin on the leg, or skin that feels warm



Note: Deep vein thrombosis should be suspected more when only one leg is swollen than when both legs are swollen.

sections.heading: Complication: Pulmonary Embolism
sections.content:
The most serious complication of deep vein thrombosis is pulmonary embolism. It occurs when a clot from a leg vein breaks off, travels through the bloodstream, and blocks a pulmonary artery.



■ Symptoms of Pulmonary Embolism

· Sudden shortness of breath

· Chest pain

· Cough (sometimes with blood)

· In severe cases, loss of consciousness or cardiac arrest can occur.



If these symptoms occur, please go to the emergency room immediately.

sections.heading: Prevention
sections.content:
The most important way to prevent it is to keep moving so that blood does not pool.

· When you have to sit for a long time, get up and move or walk your legs every 1 to 2 hours.

· On airplanes or trains, move your ankles up and down often.

· Wearing compression stockings may help blood circulation in the leg veins.

· Drink enough fluids.

· If you are recovering after surgery, it is advisable to start moving as soon as possible, following your care team's instructions.

sections.heading: Precautions
sections.content:
If one leg suddenly becomes swollen and painful, or if shortness of breath occurs, please seek medical care immediately.

Deep vein thrombosis requires treatment with anticoagulants (medications that prevent blood clots from forming), and the duration and method of treatment can vary depending on the cause. Please be sure to receive treatment according to the instructions of a medical specialist.

records.title: Heart Murmur
records.intro: A heart murmur is an extra whooshing sound heard in addition to the normal heart sounds. It is commonly detected at infant and toddler checkups and is usually a normal finding, but it can be a sign of a heart defect, so evaluation by a pediatric cardiologist is needed.
records.tags_raw: heart murmur, pediatric cardiology, echocardiogram, congenital heart disease

sections.heading: Definition
sections.content: When a doctor listens to a child's heart with a stethoscope, a whooshing or abnormal noise heard in addition to the normal thumping heartbeat is called a heart murmur. It is only a finding, not the name of a disease in itself.

sections.heading: Causes
sections.content: The most common cause is a natural sound that occurs because a growing child's blood vessels and heart are not yet fully developed (a physiologic, or innocent, murmur). Rarely, however, the sound is caused by a heart condition present from birth, such as a small hole in the heart or a valve problem.

sections.heading: Diagnosis and Treatment
sections.content: It is often found by chance during an infant health checkup or a visit for a cold. If a murmur is heard, be sure to have your child examined by a pediatric cardiologist. If needed, an echocardiogram is performed to carefully check whether any heart disease is present.

sections.heading: Precautions
sections.content: A loud murmur does not necessarily mean a dangerous, serious illness. In most cases the murmur disappears naturally as the child grows, but even if there is only a 1% chance that it is heart disease, the approach to care would change significantly, so please be sure to have your child seen at a specialty hospital.

records.title: Cardiac Arrest
records.intro: Cardiac arrest is a life-threatening emergency in which the heart stops and cannot pump blood to the body. Calling 119, prompt cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) by bystanders, and treatment by an emergency medicine specialist are key to saving the patient's life.
records.tags_raw: cardiac arrest, cardiopulmonary resuscitation, golden time, targeted temperature management, automated external defibrillator

sections.heading: Precautions
sections.content: The most important way to save a person who collapses outside a hospital is an immediate response. If you find someone who has collapsed, check whether they respond; if there is no response, call 119 right away, and if they are not breathing or not breathing normally, start cardiopulmonary resuscitation (chest compressions). The willingness of bystanders to act is essential to saving the patient's life.

sections.heading: Definition
sections.content: Cardiac arrest is a condition in which the heart does not beat properly and its pumping function stops completely. Because blood is not circulating through the body, life is at serious risk.

sections.heading: Symptoms
sections.content: When the heart stops, the person immediately collapses, loses consciousness, and stops breathing. After 4 minutes without a heartbeat, vital organs such as the brain and kidneys begin to be damaged, and after 12 minutes, the survival rate drops sharply.

sections.heading: Treatment
sections.content: When the patient arrives at the emergency room, a team of several medical staff performs chest compressions, delivers electric shocks to the heart (defibrillation), and administers medications. Even after the heart starts beating again, treatment to protect brain function by lowering body temperature to prevent brain injury (targeted temperature management) is needed for several days.

records.title: Post-Cardiac Arrest Integrated Care
records.intro: Cardiac arrest is a condition in which the heart stops, cutting off the blood supply to the brain and the rest of the body. Without emergency care within 3 to 5 minutes, serious brain damage can occur, so immediate treatment such as CPR and defibrillation is important, and integrated care by a specialized medical team is needed afterward. If cardiac arrest is suspected, call 119 immediately and receive treatment from a medical specialist.
records.tags_raw: cardiac arrest, cardiopulmonary resuscitation, defibrillation, chain of survival, targeted temperature management, heart, emergency

sections.heading: Post-Cardiac Arrest Integrated Care
sections.content:
Even after the heart starts beating again with CPR, specialized treatment is needed. This is called post-cardiac arrest integrated care.

After cardiac arrest, major organs can be damaged during the process in which the blood supply is cut off and then restored. This is called ischemia-reperfusion injury. Ischemia means a state of insufficient blood supply, and reperfusion means the return of blood supply. During this process, substances that damage cells are produced.

Integrated care includes the following:
· Treatment of the cause of the cardiac arrest
· Protection of major organs such as the brain, heart, and kidneys
· Targeted temperature management (see the section below)

The recovery process after cardiac arrest differs for each patient. Ongoing treatment and monitoring by a medical specialist are essential.

sections.heading: Targeted Temperature Management
sections.content:
Targeted temperature management is a treatment that keeps a patient's body temperature at a set level after cardiac arrest. It used to be called therapeutic hypothermia, but it was renamed targeted temperature management after studies suggested that maintaining a normal body temperature (36°C), not only a low one, can also affect treatment outcomes.

In general, treatment begins early after cardiac arrest, and the patient's body temperature is maintained at 32 to 36°C for 24 to 72 hours. This is known to help minimize brain damage and support neurological recovery.

The specific treatment approach is determined by a specialist according to the patient's condition.

sections.heading: Cardiac Arrest and the Chain of Survival
sections.content:
Cardiac arrest is a condition in which the heart suddenly stops. When the heart stops, blood (oxygen) is not supplied to major organs such as the brain, lungs, liver, and kidneys. The brain begins to be damaged 3 to 5 minutes after cardiac arrest.

The chain of survival is a step-by-step process aimed at increasing the chance of survival after cardiac arrest. It consists of the following steps, in order:
① Early recognition and calling for help (calling 119)
② Prompt CPR
③ Use of an automated external defibrillator (AED)
④ Specialized cardiac arrest treatment
⑤ Post-cardiac arrest integrated care
⑥ Rehabilitation

If even one of these is missing, the survival rate decreases. When cardiac arrest occurs outside a hospital, a quick response from people nearby is especially important.

sections.heading: What Is Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR)?
sections.content:
Cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) is emergency care performed to maintain blood circulation when cardiac arrest occurs.

Basic CPR that a lay person can perform is as follows:
· Chest compressions: press the center of the patient's chest (the lower half of the breastbone) to a depth of 5 to 6 cm at a rate of 100 to 120 compressions per minute.
· Rescue breaths: for lay people who are not healthcare professionals, performing chest compressions only is now recommended.

It is best to perform CPR after receiving professional training. It is important for everyone to learn basic CPR.

sections.heading: What Is Defibrillation?
sections.content:
Defibrillation is a treatment that delivers an electric shock to the heart. Not every patient in cardiac arrest needs defibrillation. It is performed only when ventricular fibrillation (a condition in which the heart quivers irregularly) or pulseless ventricular tachycardia (a rapid heartbeat without a pulse) is confirmed.

An automated external defibrillator (AED) installed in public places determines on its own whether defibrillation is needed and tells you. The sooner defibrillation is given, the more effective it tends to be. When you find someone in cardiac arrest, it is helpful to check where the nearest AED is located.

records.title: Intermittent Fasting
records.intro: Intermittent fasting is an eating pattern in which a person does not eat for a set period and eats only during allowed times. Short-term weight loss effects have been reported, but large-scale studies of long-term effects are still lacking. It calls for caution, or is not advisable, in certain groups such as people with diabetes mellitus, so please be sure to consult a medical specialist before starting.
records.tags_raw: intermittent fasting, diet, weight loss, calorie restriction, blood sugar, diabetes mellitus, eating disorder, pregnancy, eating pattern, anxious feeling in the chest, restlessness, worrying for no reason

sections.heading: Effects of Intermittent Fasting
sections.content:
Intermittent fasting is an eating method that divides time into an eating window and a fasting window. Typical examples include eating only during 8 hours a day and fasting for 16 hours (the 16:8 method), and eating very little on only 2 days a week (the 5:2 method).



■ Weight Loss Effects

In the short term, reducing energy intake may help with weight loss. However, the effect is similar to that of ordinary calorie-restricted diets, and long-term studies in large populations are still lacking.



■ Health Effects

Studies in animals and in some people have reported positive effects such as improved blood sugar, lower blood pressure, improved insulin sensitivity (how responsive the body is to insulin), and reduced inflammation. However, evidence that it is superior to other weight loss methods is not yet clear.

sections.heading: When to Avoid Intermittent Fasting
sections.content:
If any of the following apply to you, please be sure to consult a medical specialist before starting intermittent fasting. In general, it is not recommended in the following cases:



- People with diabetes mellitus

- People with heart, kidney, or liver disease

- Growing children and adolescents under 18 years of age

- People who have, or have a history of, an eating disorder (anorexia nervosa, bulimia nervosa)

- People who are pregnant or breastfeeding

- People with low blood pressure



Intermittent fasting should be avoided in conditions in which skipping meals can cause health problems such as unstable blood sugar and nutritional imbalance.

sections.heading: How to Practice It Properly
sections.content:
■ First Check Whether It Suits You

Benefits may be expected only if intermittent fasting is easier for you to stick with than counting calories every day. Think first about whether this is a method you can keep up over the long term.



■ Key Point: Do Not Overeat During the Allowed Time

The basis of weight loss is eating less than the calories you burn. It helps to plan and prepare in advance the food you will eat during your eating window.



■ Maintain Nutritional Balance

When the eating window is shortened, vitamins and minerals may become insufficient. During the allowed eating time, pay even more attention to eating a balanced meal made from healthy ingredients.



■ Conclusion

What you eat matters more than the pattern in which you eat. Intermittent fasting is not suitable for everyone, so please choose a method that suits you after consulting a medical specialist.



※ The information in this Health Encyclopedia is for reference purposes only. For accurate diagnosis and treatment, please consult a medical specialist.

records.title: Adenovirus Infection
records.intro: Adenovirus is a virus that can cause infection in several parts of the body, including the respiratory tract, the eyes (conjunctiva), and the gastrointestinal tract. It mainly affects children, and infections occur throughout the year. Most cases recover with supportive (symptomatic) treatment, but people with weakened immunity can develop severe pneumonia, so caution is needed.

sections.heading: Definition
sections.content:
Adenovirus is a virus that can cause infection in various parts of the body, including the respiratory tract, the conjunctiva (the surface of the eye), and the gastrointestinal (digestive) tract. It mainly affects children but can also infect adults.



It occurs throughout the year, and infection without symptoms (asymptomatic infection) is also common. Outbreaks can occur in settings where people live or gather in groups.

sections.heading: Symptoms
sections.content:
Adenovirus causes a variety of symptoms depending on the site of infection.



· Respiratory symptoms: sore throat, fever, and cough. In severe cases, it can progress to pneumonia and may look similar to bacterial pneumonia.

· Conjunctivitis: red eyes and a foreign body sensation. Symptoms are relatively mild, but it is highly contagious and can cause outbreaks.

· Gastroenteritis: can cause acute diarrhea in children, and most cases resolve on their own.

· Hemorrhagic cystitis: hematuria (blood in the urine), dysuria (pain when urinating), and urinary frequency (urinating often) can last 1 to 2 weeks. It occurs in children and young adults.



If symptoms persist or worsen, please consult a medical specialist.

sections.heading: Treatment
sections.content:
Adenovirus infection is mostly treated with supportive (symptomatic) care. Supportive care is treatment that relieves symptoms such as fever and cough.



Getting enough rest and fluids can help. Currently, the specific antiviral drugs available in Korea are limited.



In people with weakened immunity (such as those receiving cancer treatment or taking immunosuppressants after an organ transplant), the infection can lead to severe pneumonia, so in these cases, please consult a medical specialist right away.

records.title: Cellulitis
records.intro: Cellulitis is an infection that occurs when bacteria invade the dermis (the middle layer of the skin) and the subcutaneous fat layer. It can cause the skin to become red and swollen, along with fever and pain. If you have symptoms, you should see a medical specialist promptly.
records.tags_raw: cellulitis, soft tissue infection, bacterial infection, skin infection, antibiotics, athlete's foot, lymphangitis, body swelling, facial swelling, leg swelling, swelling in hands and feet

sections.heading: Preventing Recurrence
sections.content:
If you have had cellulitis once, you are more likely to have a recurrence if you have the following risk factors:

· Athlete's foot (tinea pedis), lymphedema (a condition in which lymph fluid builds up and causes swelling), diabetes mellitus, obesity, smoking, skin ulcers

To prevent recurrence, these underlying conditions need to be treated. Please consult a medical specialist to confirm how to manage them.

sections.heading: Causes
sections.content:
Cellulitis is mainly caused by the bacteria Staphylococcus aureus and Streptococcus pyogenes.

· The most common route is bacteria entering through cracks between the toes caused by athlete's foot and similar conditions.

· Infection can also occur through areas of existing skin conditions such as folliculitis, boils, wounds, ulcers, and eczema.

· Bacteria can also enter through injuries, surgical sites, or insect bites.

sections.heading: Symptoms
sections.content:
· Characteristic features are pale pink patches, swelling (edema), warmth, tenderness (pain when pressed), and pain.

· The erythema (red patch) can spread relatively quickly, by about 2 to 10 cm per day.

· Blisters or pus may form, or the center may fester and rupture.

· When it occurs on an arm or leg, a red streak can extend along the lymphatic vessels (the channels through which lymph fluid flows), and the lymph nodes may swell.

· In severe cases, it can progress to sepsis (a condition in which bacteria spread through the bloodstream) or skin necrosis.

sections.heading: Treatment
sections.content:
· Antibiotics are the basic treatment.

· In some cases, a short course of steroids is used together with them.

· When it occurs in the leg, elevating the leg and wearing compression stockings are recommended.

· Cold compresses can help relieve pain and swelling.

records.title: Atopic Dermatitis
records.intro: Atopic dermatitis is a chronic skin condition in which allergic mechanisms cause ongoing inflammation of the skin. It causes severe itching and recurring eczema, and the skin can become thick and rough (lichenification). It tends to occur when a person with a genetic predisposition is exposed to allergy triggers, and symptoms can worsen with spring pollen, house dust mites, and fine particulate matter. If symptoms persist, please consult an allergist or a dermatologist.
records.tags_raw: atopic dermatitis, allergy, itching, eczema, pollen, house dust mites, moisturizing, steroid ointment

sections.heading: Symptoms
sections.content:
The main symptoms of atopic dermatitis are as follows:

· Severe itching: often worse at night, interfering with sleep.
· Eczema: the skin becomes red, oozes fluid, or forms crusts.
· Dry skin
· Repeated cycles of flare-ups and improvement

Infants (2 months to 2 years): it often appears first on the cheeks, forehead, and scalp.
Children and adolescents: it commonly appears in skin folds such as the inner elbows, behind the knees, and the neck.
Adults: it commonly appears on the face, neck, and hands.

In spring, higher pollen and fine particulate matter levels can make symptoms worse.

sections.heading: Prevention and Lifestyle Management
sections.content:
Lifestyle guidelines to help prevent flare-ups of atopic dermatitis are as follows.

■ Avoiding Allergy Triggers
· On days when the pollen count is high, keep windows closed to reduce the amount of pollen entering indoors.
· Check fine particulate matter levels with a smartphone app or similar, and wear a mask when going outside.
· Using an air purifier can help lower indoor pollen and fine particulate matter levels.
· Wash bedding often, and use dust mite–proof covers.
· Reduce the use of fabric sofas, curtains, and carpets whenever possible.
· Keep indoor temperature and humidity appropriate, and ventilate often.

■ Nutrition
· Vitamin D may help strengthen immune function and help prevent the progression of allergies. It is good to get it from oily fish, eggs, and milk, or through appropriate sun exposure.
· Omega-3 fatty acids (found in mackerel, salmon, walnuts, etc.) may help reduce inflammation.
· Eating vegetables and fruits with antioxidant effects is also recommended.

sections.heading: Treatment
sections.content:
Treatment of atopic dermatitis combines avoiding trigger substances with medication.

■ Medication
· Steroid ointments, lotions, and creams: the most basic treatment for reducing skin inflammation. They must be used on the appropriate areas and at the appropriate strength according to a specialist's instructions.
· Immunomodulators: used as an alternative when long-term steroid use is difficult.
· Oral antihistamines: can help relieve itching.

■ Moisturizing
Applying enough moisturizer within 3 minutes after a shower is very important for maintaining the skin barrier. Use a gentle moisturizer consistently at least twice a day.

■ Immunotherapy
This method gradually injects the causative allergen under the skin (subcutaneously), starting from a low concentration and increasing slowly. It reduces the immune response and may help control symptoms over the long term.

Even when symptoms improve, continuing treatment steadily is important for preventing recurrence. Please be sure to consult a medical specialist.

sections.heading: Causes
sections.content:
Atopic dermatitis occurs or worsens when a person with a genetic predisposition to allergies is exposed to the following environments.

■ Major Allergy Triggers
· House dust mites: they multiply readily in warm, humid environments. Urbanized indoor environments favor their growth.
· Pollen: concentrations rise in spring, which often worsens symptoms.
· Pet hair and dander
· Mold and cockroaches
· Certain foods

■ Other Aggravating Factors
· Air pollutants such as fine particulate matter
· Stress
· Dry environments
· Sweat

It is important to find out which substances you react to through testing (skin allergy testing or blood tests).

sections.heading: Definition
sections.content:
Atopic dermatitis is a condition in which an allergic immune response causes chronic inflammation of the skin. Atopy refers to a genetic tendency to develop allergic diseases.

The main features are as follows:
· Severe itching
· Recurrent eczema (skin changes that are red and oozing or crusted)
· If it lasts a long time, the skin becomes thick and rough (lichenification)

Atopic dermatitis often occurs together with other allergic conditions (such as allergic rhinitis and asthma). Having a family member with an allergic condition increases the likelihood of developing it.

records.title: Malignant Melanoma
records.intro: Malignant melanoma is a malignant tumor that develops from melanocytes in the skin or mucous membranes. Melanocytes are the cells that produce skin pigment. Its prognosis tends to be the poorest among skin cancers, so early detection is very important. If you notice any unusual change in your skin, please be sure to consult a dermatologist.
records.tags_raw: malignant melanoma, melanoma, skin cancer, melanin, skin, mole, pigment

sections.heading: Definition
sections.content: This is a malignant tumor that develops from melanocytes in the skin or mucous membranes. Melanocytes are the cells that produce skin pigment (melanin). Its prognosis tends to be the poorest among skin cancers, so early detection is very important. The number of cases in Korea is gradually increasing.

sections.heading: Diagnosis and Treatment
sections.content: It is diagnosed through an examination by a dermatologist and a biopsy. Surgical removal of the lesion is the basic treatment. If the cancer has spread to other sites, immunotherapy, targeted therapy, radiation therapy, and other treatments may also be needed. Please discuss the treatment approach thoroughly with your doctor.

sections.heading: Symptoms and Self-Examination
sections.content:
In the early stages, there are almost no symptoms such as itching or pain, so detection can be delayed. Be alert for the following changes:
· Asymmetry: one half of the mole looks different from the other half
· Irregular border: the edge of the mole is jagged or blurred
· Color change: several colors are mixed within the mole
· Size: a diameter of 6 mm or more
· Change: changes in surface condition, such as pain, bleeding, crusting, or ulceration
If you notice an unusual mole on your skin, it helps to take a photo and record any changes over time.

sections.heading: Causes and Sites of Occurrence
sections.content: Ultraviolet exposure, genetic factors, and trauma (injury) are presumed to be causes. In Korea, cases occurring on the soles, palms, and fingers and toes, which have little UV exposure, account for about 60% of all cases. It is sometimes mistaken for a wart or a foot ulcer (a wound on the foot), causing treatment to be delayed.

sections.heading: Precautions
sections.content: Be careful not to miss the right time for treatment by mistaking it for a wart, a foot ulcer, or a wound. If you have an area of skin that does not heal for a long time or that keeps changing, please be sure to consult a dermatologist. Early detection is very important for improving the outlook.

records.title: Dry Eye Disease
records.intro: Dry eye disease is a condition in which the surface of the eye becomes dry because there are not enough tears or the tears evaporate too quickly. It causes a variety of symptoms, such as stinging, dryness, and a feeling that something is in the eye. If symptoms are severe or persist, please consult an ophthalmology specialist.
records.tags_raw: dry eye disease, dry eye, tears, foreign body sensation, artificial tears, blepharitis, lack of energy, listlessness, persistent tiredness, anxious feeling, nervousness, worrying for no reason

sections.heading: Definition
sections.content: Dry eye disease is a condition in which tears are not produced well, or tears evaporate too quickly, making the tear film on the surface of the eye unstable. Tears keep the surface of the eye moist and protect the eye from external irritants. When tears are insufficient, inflammation and damage can develop on the surface of the eye.

sections.heading: Symptoms
sections.content:
Dry eye disease can cause a variety of symptoms.

· Foreign body sensation: A feeling as if grains of sand are rolling in the eye

· Burning: A feeling as if soapy water has gotten into the eye

· Dry, gritty feeling and eye fatigue

· Stringy, sticky eye discharge

· Stinging or aching that makes it hard to open the eyes

· Temporary blurred vision



Symptoms are especially severe during the spring and autumn seasonal changes and in winter. Paradoxically, excessive tearing can also be caused by dry eye disease, because when the dry surface of the eye is irritated, the eye reflexively produces a large amount of tears.



If symptoms continue, please consult a medical specialist.

sections.heading: Causes
sections.content:
There are many causes of dry eye disease.

· Aging: Tear production may decrease with age.

· Systemic diseases: Sjogren's syndrome, rheumatoid arthritis, diabetes, thyroid disease, and others

· Hormonal changes: Dryness can worsen because of hormonal changes, especially in women.

· Medications: Some medications can affect tear production.

· Environment: Dry weather, strong wind, fine dust, and use of air conditioning or heating

· Reduced blinking: Blinking decreases during long periods of smartphone or computer use, causing the eyes to dry out quickly.

· Eye makeup: Mascara, eyeliner, and similar products can block the oil glands of the eyelids and cause dryness.



In winter, indoor air becomes dry because of heating, and in spring, symptoms worsen because of yellow dust and fine dust.

sections.heading: Diagnosis
sections.content:
The following tests are performed to diagnose dry eye disease.

· Tear film breakup time test: Measures how quickly the tears disappear from the surface of the eye after a blink.

· Tear production test

· Tear osmolarity test

· Ocular surface inflammation test



As a self-check, if you open your eyes wide and hold them without blinking for 10 seconds and your eyes sting or hurt badly, dry eye disease may be suspected. In this case, please consult an ophthalmology specialist for an accurate examination.

sections.heading: Treatment
sections.content:
The basis of dry eye treatment is the use of artificial tear eye drops. Artificial tears moisten the surface of the eye, dilute inflammatory substances, and help regenerate damaged cells.



· Artificial tears: If they are needed 5 to 6 or more times a day, preservative-free single-use artificial tears are used.

· Anti-inflammatory eye drops: When inflammation is severe, eye drops that control inflammation are used as prescribed by a specialist.

· Punctal occlusion: A procedure that blocks the opening through which tears drain, so that tears stay on the eye longer.

· Warm eyelid compresses and eyelid cleansing: Help the oil glands of the eyelids function properly to reduce tear evaporation.



Using tap water as a substitute for artificial tears is dangerous because it can expose the eye to microorganisms that cause keratitis (corneal infection).

sections.heading: Prevention
sections.content:
The following measures can help prevent dry eye disease.

· Keep indoor humidity at 40 to 60%. Use a humidifier.

· Keep air from air conditioners and heaters from blowing directly on your eyes.

· When using a smartphone or computer, consciously blink often and take a break every 20 to 30 minutes.

· Use artificial tears regularly.

· Get enough sleep and quit smoking.

· When going out on a day with strong sunlight, protect your eyes with sunglasses or a hat.



If symptoms are severe or continue, please consult an ophthalmology specialist.

records.title: Allergic Conjunctivitis
records.intro: Allergic conjunctivitis is a condition in which the conjunctiva of the eye becomes inflamed in response to allergens such as pollen and fine dust. It is characterized by itchy, red eyes. If symptoms are severe or persist, please consult an ophthalmology specialist.
records.tags_raw: allergic conjunctivitis, allergy, itchy eyes, red eyes, pollen, conjunctivitis, stuffy nose, clear runny nose, yellow runny nose

sections.heading: Definition
sections.content: The conjunctiva is the thin membrane that covers the inside of the eyelids and the white of the eye. Allergic conjunctivitis is a condition in which the conjunctiva reacts to allergens such as pollen, yellow dust, fine dust, and house dust, causing inflammation. It is sometimes called a 'cold of the eye.' It occurs especially often during the spring and autumn seasonal changes.

sections.heading: Symptoms
sections.content:
The main symptoms of allergic conjunctivitis are as follows.

· Itchy eyes: The most characteristic symptom of allergic conjunctivitis.

· Redness: The eyes turn red.

· Sensitivity to light

· Sticky eye discharge

· Tearing



Allergic rhinitis (runny nose, sneezing) or atopic dermatitis often occurs together with it. Most cases resolve without any particular aftereffects, but if the condition becomes severe, complications that reduce vision can develop, so caution is needed.

sections.heading: Treatment
sections.content:
The most important thing in treating allergic conjunctivitis is not to rub the eyes. Rubbing the eyes causes more of the substances that trigger the allergic reaction to be released, which worsens symptoms.



· Eye drops: Use anti-allergy eye drops prescribed by a specialist.

· Artificial tears: Dilute or wash away allergens.

· Cold compresses: Relieve swelling and itching.



If symptoms continue, please consult an ophthalmology specialist.

sections.heading: Prevention
sections.content:
· Limit going outdoors when pollen counts are high, and wash your hands thoroughly after coming back inside.

· Do not rub your eyes with your hands.

· Wear glasses instead of contact lenses.

· When ventilating a room, take care to keep pollen from coming indoors.

records.title: Allergic Rhinitis
records.intro: Allergic rhinitis is a condition in which the nasal mucosa reacts excessively to certain substances (allergens). The main symptoms are sudden bouts of sneezing, clear runny nose, stuffy nose, and itching. According to the Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey, about 18% of Koreans experience it. The incidence is especially high among teenagers. If symptoms persist or complications are suspected, please consult an otolaryngology (ENT) specialist.
records.tags_raw: allergic rhinitis, rhinitis, sneezing, runny nose, nasal congestion, house dust mites, pollen, seasonal change, headache, splitting headache, migraine, pain at the back of the head, stuffy nose, clear runny nose, yellow runny nose
keywords: pain at the back of the head

sections.heading: Definition
sections.content:
Allergic rhinitis is a condition in which the nasal mucosa reacts excessively to certain substances (allergens), such as pollen, house dust mites, and dust. It occurs often during the spring and autumn seasonal changes and tends to peak in September.



Symptoms worsen during seasonal changes because of sudden temperature changes. Temperature changes dry out the nasal mucosa, and exposure to cold air causes nasal congestion. A large daily temperature range makes the airways more sensitive and can make symptoms worse.

sections.heading: Symptoms
sections.content:
The typical symptoms of allergic rhinitis are as follows.



· Repeated, sudden bouts of sneezing

· Clear runny nose that keeps flowing

· Itching around the eyes and nose

· Nasal congestion



The following symptoms may also occur.

· Itching or pain in the eyes, roof of the mouth, or throat

· Frequent tearing

· Headache and reduced sense of smell

· Nosebleeds caused by nasal irritation



Complications include sinusitis (inflammation of the air spaces in the bones around the nose), nasal polyps, otitis media (middle ear infection), sleep disturbance, and asthma. In children, chronic nasal congestion leads to mouth breathing, which can cause dental malocclusion and changes in the shape of the face.

sections.heading: Treatment
sections.content:
There are four main approaches to treating allergic rhinitis.



■ Environmental Therapy (Avoidance Therapy)

The causative substance is first identified through allergy testing. This approach involves avoiding exposure to the identified substance.



■ Drug Therapy

Antihistamines, which block histamine (a substance that causes allergy symptoms) involved in the allergic reaction, are mainly used. Their effect appears within about 1 hour of taking them. For severe symptoms, intranasal steroid sprays may also be used.



■ Immunotherapy

It is considered when short-term drug treatment is not enough. This treatment regulates the immune response to the causative substance. It takes about 6 months to 1 year for its effect to appear. There are two methods: subcutaneous injection and sublingual administration, in which medication is placed under the tongue.



■ Surgical Therapy

It may be tried when the tissue inside the nose (the inferior turbinates) has become enlarged because of allergic rhinitis and nasal congestion is severe. Options include radiofrequency reduction of the inferior turbinates and inferior turbinectomy (surgical removal of the turbinates).



The treatment method is determined by a specialist based on the patient's condition. Please be sure to consult an otolaryngology (ENT) specialist.

sections.heading: Prevention
sections.content:
These are lifestyle guidelines to help prevent allergic rhinitis and reduce symptoms.



■ Managing House Dust Mites

· Wash bedding once every 1 to 2 weeks in hot water at 55°C or higher.

· Cover pillows and duvets with dust mite-proof covers.

· Keep the indoor temperature at 18 to 23°C and the relative humidity at 40 to 50%.

· Clean the house often and replace air purifier filters on time.



■ Personal Hygiene

· Change your mask after going outside.

· Wash your hands with soap under running water for at least 30 seconds.



■ Fluid Intake

· Drink 1.5 to 2 liters of water a day. Adequate fluid intake helps keep the nasal mucosa from drying out.

· Lukewarm or warm water is more helpful than cold water.

records.title: Alcoholism (Alcohol Use Disorder)
records.intro: Alcoholism (alcohol use disorder) is a chronic mental health condition in which drinking beyond socially accepted levels impairs physical, psychological, and social functioning. It results from a loss of the brain's control over drinking, not from a lack of willpower. Recovery may be possible with professional treatment, so please do not hesitate to ask for help.
records.tags_raw: alcoholism, alcohol use disorder, drinking, alcohol abstinence, detoxification treatment, sobriety, relapse prevention, craving, hand tremor, body tremor, anxious feeling, nervousness, worrying for no reason

sections.heading: Causes
sections.content:
Alcoholism results from an interaction between genetic factors (about 60%) and environmental factors (about 40%).

· Genetic factors: Family members of people with alcoholism have a 3 to 4 times higher risk of alcohol-related problems.

· Psychological factors: Repeated drinking to relieve tension, boost energy, or ease psychological distress can lead to addiction.

· Environmental and sociocultural factors: A social atmosphere that is tolerant of drinking, the age at which drinking begins, and easy access to alcohol also have an influence.

sections.heading: Diagnosis
sections.content:
Alcohol use disorder is diagnosed when 2 or more of the following 11 criteria have applied during the past 12 months.

① Drinking more, or for longer, than intended.

② Trying to cut down or stop drinking but being unsuccessful.

③ Spending a great deal of time obtaining alcohol, drinking, or recovering from its effects.

④ Having a strong desire (craving) to drink.

⑤ Failing to fulfill responsibilities at work, school, or home because of repeated drinking.

⑥ Having relationship problems because of drinking.

⑦ Giving up important social or occupational activities because of drinking.

⑧ Drinking in situations that are physically dangerous (for example, drunk driving).

⑨ Continuing to drink despite physical or psychological problems.

⑩ Developing tolerance, in which the amount of alcohol needed gradually increases.

⑪ Experiencing withdrawal symptoms, such as being unable to sleep or feeling anxious, when stopping drinking.



2 to 3 criteria: Mild / 4 to 5 criteria: Moderate / 6 or more criteria: Severe



■ Brief Screening Questions (CAGE)

① Have you ever tried to cut down or stop drinking?

② Have you ever felt annoyed because people around you were worried about or criticized your drinking?

③ Have you ever felt guilty about your drinking?

④ Have you ever had a drink to relieve a hangover?

If you answer 'yes' to 2 or more, please consult a professional.

sections.heading: Treatment
sections.content:
Treatment of alcoholism proceeds in stages.



■ Stage 1: Detoxification

This stage treats the withdrawal symptoms (anxiety, insomnia, tremor, and others) that occur when drinking stops. It usually takes about 2 weeks, and hospital treatment is needed when symptoms are severe. Vitamins and nutrition are replaced through intravenous fluids, and antianxiety medication is given.



■ Stage 2: Maintenance Treatment (Staying Alcohol-Free)

· Drug treatment: Anti-craving medication is used to suppress the desire and urges to drink.

· Psychological treatment: Alcohol education, motivational enhancement therapy, cognitive behavioral therapy, relapse prevention therapy, family therapy, and other approaches are provided.



Relapse is common, but this does not mean recovery is impossible. Like high blood pressure and diabetes, it is a chronic condition that requires ongoing management and treatment. Maintaining sobriety for 1 year or longer may improve the chances of recovery.

sections.heading: Coping with Cravings
sections.content:
■ Lifestyle Guidelines

· Remove all alcohol from the home.

· Do not attend work dinners or gatherings where alcohol is served.

· Avoid walking past the stores or bars where you used to buy or drink alcohol.

· Tell family and friends confidently that you are abstaining from alcohol.



■ The 4D Technique When a Craving Occurs

① Delay: Put off the act of drinking.

② Deep breath: Take a deep breath.

③ Drink water: Take a sip of water.

④ Do anything else: Chew gum, squeeze a stress ball, or do another activity.



A craving comes on strongly for a short time, like a wave, and then passes. If you hold out for just a few minutes, it becomes more manageable.



When refusing a drink at a social gathering, say 'no' clearly from the start, and make toasts with another drink, such as lemon-lime soda.

sections.heading: Available Resources
sections.content:
· Mental Health Welfare Centers (operated by each city, county, and district): Provide counseling and programs

· Addiction Management Integrated Support Centers (49 locations nationwide): Provide counseling for patients and families and a variety of programs

· Psychiatry (clinics, specialized alcohol hospitals, and university hospitals): Drug treatment and psychological treatment

· Alcoholics Anonymous (AA): A self-help group of peers who are in recovery



You do not have to go through treatment and recovery alone. Please actively seek help.

records.title: Drug Allergy
records.intro: Drug allergy is a condition in which an allergic reaction occurs after taking a medication. Reactions range from mild ones, such as hives, to life-threatening anaphylaxis. It is important to identify the causative medication accurately and to inform your care team.
records.tags_raw: drug allergy, anaphylaxis, hives, adverse drug reaction, antibiotic allergy, diagnosis, prevention, shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, labored breathing, feeling of suffocation, body swelling, facial swelling, leg swelling, swollen hands and feet

sections.heading: Definition
sections.content:
An adverse drug reaction is the appearance of unwanted symptoms rather than the therapeutic effect of a medication. A drug allergy is an adverse drug reaction that occurs through an immune response (an allergic mechanism).



For example, feeling drowsy or having heartburn after taking cold medicine is an adverse drug reaction but not an allergy. Hives over the whole body after an antibiotic injection is a drug allergy. Because it is difficult for the general public to tell the two apart accurately, please be sure to consult a doctor.

sections.heading: Symptoms and Dangerous Situations
sections.content:
Drug allergy ranges from mild hives to life-threatening reactions.



■ Serious Reactions to Watch For

· Anaphylaxis: Hives, swelling of the face and arms, decreased level of consciousness, difficulty breathing, and low blood pressure appear suddenly. You must go to the emergency room immediately.

· Stevens-Johnson syndrome: Blisters and a severe rash appear on the skin. It is very dangerous.

· Reduced function of the liver, heart, and kidneys



If any abnormal symptoms appear, seek immediate medical attention.

sections.heading: Diagnosis
sections.content:
The most important step is to identify the causative medication accurately.

· Check the ingredients of the medication you took from the prescription or the product's brand name.

· Allergy skin tests and blood antibody tests

· Oral challenge test (taking a small amount of the drug to check for a reaction): Performed under the supervision of an allergy specialist.



If you are hypersensitive to an anti-inflammatory pain reliever (NSAID) such as ibuprofen, you may also react to other NSAIDs. This is called cross-reactivity. Please discuss alternative medications, such as acetaminophen (Tylenol) or celecoxib, with a specialist.

sections.heading: Prevention
sections.content:
· Learn the exact name of the active ingredient of the causative medication.

· Be sure to tell your doctor or pharmacist whenever you receive a prescription in the future.

· Have the drug allergy recorded in your hospital medical record, or obtain a drug safety card.



■ Adverse Drug Reaction Relief System

If a person dies, becomes disabled, or requires hospital treatment because of a drug adverse reaction, an application can be made to the Korea Institute of Drug Safety & Risk Management, and eligible cases may receive government support, including a lump-sum death benefit, funeral expenses, a lump-sum disability benefit, and hospitalization costs.

records.title: Shoulder Pain
records.intro: The main causes of shoulder pain are rotator cuff tear, adhesive capsulitis (frozen shoulder), calcific tendinitis, and cervical radiculopathy. Because treatment differs depending on the cause, an accurate diagnosis is important. If shoulder pain persists, please consult a medical specialist.
records.tags_raw: shoulder pain, rotator cuff tear, frozen shoulder, adhesive capsulitis, calcific tendinitis, cervical radiculopathy, glenohumeral arthritis, arthroscopic surgery

sections.heading: Diagnosis
sections.content:
Shoulder pain has many possible causes and is difficult to tell apart based on symptoms alone. After a consultation with a shoulder specialist, the cause can be identified in most cases with X-ray and ultrasound examinations, and MRI is performed selectively when necessary.

■ Self-Assessment Reference
· Pain when moving the shoulder → possible rotator cuff disease, calcific tendinitis, or adhesive capsulitis
· Reduced range of motion, or pain only at the end of the range of motion → possible adhesive capsulitis
· Pain that is unrelated to movement and changes when lying down or with neck position → possible cervical radiculopathy

Self-assessment is for reference only. For an accurate diagnosis, please consult a medical specialist; imaging tests are also needed.

sections.heading: Causes
sections.content:
The four main causes of shoulder pain are as follows.

· Rotator cuff tear: A degenerative condition in which the muscles that surround the shoulder joint (the rotator cuff) tear.
· Adhesive capsulitis (frozen shoulder): A condition in which the shoulder joint capsule becomes inflamed and stiff, which can occur from the age of 40 onward.
· Calcific tendinitis: A condition in which calcium deposits build up in the shoulder tendons, causing inflammation and pain.
· Cervical radiculopathy: A condition in which a nerve is compressed by a herniated neck disc or degenerative changes, causing pain that extends to the shoulder.

sections.heading: Treatment
sections.content:
■ Non-Surgical Treatment
· Glenohumeral arthritis (inflammation of the shoulder joint): Anti-inflammatory pain relievers and medications that support cartilage are used first, and injection therapy is added when necessary.
· Rheumatoid arthritis: Drug treatment (including biologics) comes first, and injection therapy is used if there is no response.
· Adhesive capsulitis: Most cases may improve with stretching and conservative treatment.
· Calcific tendinitis: Most cases are treated without surgery.

■ Surgery
Arthroscopic surgery is considered in the following cases.
· Full-thickness rotator cuff tear: When the tear is progressing or is a full-thickness tear, surgery is recommended, especially for people whose jobs involve heavy use of the arms, because the tear is more likely to worsen.
· Calcific tendinitis: Performed only in limited cases, such as when the calcific deposit is very large or the pain is severe.
· Adhesive capsulitis: Considered only when there is no response to conservative treatment.

Most shoulder surgeries are performed using an arthroscope (a type of endoscope). After rotator cuff repair, an arm sling is used for about 6 weeks, recovery management is needed for up to 3 months, and exercise may be possible from about 6 months after surgery.

sections.heading: Prevention
sections.content:
· Making stretching a daily habit can help prevent the three major shoulder conditions (rotator cuff tear, frozen shoulder, and calcific tendinitis).
· Stretch thoroughly before exercising, and avoid sudden, strenuous exercise.
· Working for long periods with the arms raised above shoulder height can damage the shoulder. Improving the work environment or changing posture can help.
· If you have rheumatoid arthritis, it is important to keep up with drug treatment and manage the condition before joint damage occurs.
· There is no direct link between diet and shoulder pain, so you may eat a balanced variety of foods.

records.title: Tinea Versicolor (Pityriasis Versicolor)
records.intro: Tinea versicolor (pityriasis versicolor) is a skin condition in which a fungus called Malassezia overgrows on the skin and causes patchy, uneven spots. It tends to occur in summer, when people sweat a lot. If symptoms persist, please consult a dermatology specialist.
records.tags_raw: tinea versicolor, pityriasis versicolor, fungus, fungal infection, skin, spots, summer

sections.heading: Symptoms
sections.content: It mainly occurs on areas with heavy sebum (skin oil) production, such as the chest, back, and armpits. Patchy spots with a change in skin color appear on the skin.

sections.heading: Prevention
sections.content: After sweating, it is important to shower right away and keep the skin clean and dry.

sections.heading: Definition
sections.content: It is a condition in which a fungus called Malassezia overgrows on the skin, causing changes in skin color and patchy spots. It is also called pityriasis versicolor ('jeonpung' in Korean).

sections.heading: Treatment
sections.content: If symptoms persist or are severe, please consult a dermatology specialist and receive antifungal treatment.

records.title: Dizziness
records.intro: Dizziness is a general term for a feeling that the surroundings are spinning or that it is hard to keep your balance. It may be caused by something simple, such as anemia or an ear problem, but it can also be a sign of a dangerous brain condition. Because the exact cause must be found and treated, please be sure to consult a medical specialist for an examination.
records.tags_raw: dizziness, vertigo, balance disorder, cerebral infarction, orthostatic hypotension, headache, splitting headache, migraine, pain at the back of the head, lightheadedness, spinning sensation, unsteadiness, vision going dark, collapse, loss of consciousness, fainting, weakness in the arms or legs, difficulty moving one side of the body, anxious feeling, nervousness, worrying for no reason
keywords: pain at the back of the head
weakness in the arms or legs
difficulty moving one side of the body

sections.heading: Causes
sections.content:
To keep the body balanced and upright, the organs of the inner ear (the peripheral nervous system) and the brain (the central nervous system) must work together. The cause of dizziness differs depending on which of these two areas has a problem.



There are also many other causes, including heart problems, anemia, 'orthostatic hypotension' (in which blood does not reach the brain quickly enough when standing up after sitting), and psychological problems such as anxiety or panic disorder.

sections.heading: Types
sections.content:
The type of condition can sometimes be guessed from how the dizziness feels.



· Vertigo (rotational): A feeling that the world or your own body is spinning. You may also feel as if you are going to vomit, and it mainly occurs when there is a problem in the ear.

· Balance disorder: If there is no spinning sensation but you stagger like a drunk person and feel you might fall to one side, there is a high possibility that a blood vessel in the brain (the cerebellum) has become blocked or has ruptured.

· Presyncopal dizziness: A feeling that your vision is going dark and you are about to faint. It is common in people with orthostatic hypotension or anemia.

· Psychogenic dizziness: If you feel as if you are floating or detached from your body and break out in a cold sweat, a psychological problem (such as an anxiety disorder) is likely.

sections.heading: Symptoms to Watch For
sections.content:
If any of the following symptoms occur together with dizziness, it may be a very dangerous condition such as 'cerebral infarction (stroke),' so you should go to the emergency room without delay.



· A severe headache, so severe that you think, 'I have never had a headache this bad'

· Weakness or a sense of paralysis in one arm or leg

· Slurred speech or difficulty swallowing

· Double vision or blurred vision

In this case, raise both arms in front of you and check whether only one arm suddenly drops.

records.title: Hallux Valgus (Bunion)
records.intro: Hallux valgus is a deformity in which the big toe tilts toward the second toe. It tends to develop with prolonged wearing of shoes that are narrow or pointed at the toe, or high heels. As the deformity progresses, various complications can develop, so please consult a medical specialist.
records.tags_raw: hallux valgus, bunion, high heels, foot deformity, forefoot width, transverse arch, foot and ankle

sections.heading: Treatment
sections.content:
Treatment of hallux valgus depends on the severity of the deformity.
· Early stage: Switch to shoes that are wide in the forefoot and round at the toe, and wear an orthotic device prescribed by a specialist. Perform toe-spreading exercises. However, caution is needed because pulling the big toe directly with your fingers can actually worsen the deformity.
· Severe cases: Surgical treatment may be needed when the deformity is severe.
Please consult a medical specialist before deciding on a treatment method.

sections.heading: Definition
sections.content: Hallux valgus is a deformity in which the big toe tilts toward the second toe at the joint at the base of the big toe.

sections.heading: Symptoms
sections.content: The forefoot becomes wider, and the inner side of the base of the big toe protrudes and rubs against the shoe, causing pain. As the transverse arch of the foot (the arch that runs across the front of the foot) collapses, calluses may also form on the sole at the base of the second, third, and fourth toes. Calluses can also form on the top of the toes as the toes overlap or bend inside narrow shoes.

sections.heading: Causes
sections.content:
The most common cause is wearing shoes that are narrow or pointed at the toe, or high-heeled shoes, for long periods. Wearing high heels shifts body weight forward, causing the transverse arch of the foot to collapse, and the narrow toe box gradually pushes the big toe to tilt.
Genetic factors may also play a role. The prevalence is known to be high among women in their 30s and older in Korea.

sections.heading: Prevention
sections.content:
To help prevent hallux valgus, it is important to wear shoes that are wide in the forefoot and round at the toe. It is best to avoid, as far as possible, high heels with a heel height of more than 3 cm.
If you must wear high heels, it helps to take your shoes off often and do toe-spreading exercises.

records.title: Cerebrovascular Disease (Stroke)
records.intro: Cerebrovascular disease (stroke) is a condition in which a blood vessel in the brain becomes blocked or ruptures, causing brain damage. To minimize aftereffects, prompt emergency response is most important, under the principle that 'time is brain.' The risk of stroke is especially high in winter and during seasonal changes, so please follow the prevention guidelines carefully.
records.tags_raw: stroke, cerebral infarction, cerebral hemorrhage, thrombolysis, thrombectomy, cerebrovascular disease, winter stroke, first aid, post-stroke sequelae, multidisciplinary care, headache, splitting headache, migraine, pain at the back of the head, lightheadedness, spinning sensation, unsteadiness, vision going dark, weakness in the arms or legs, difficulty moving one side of the body
keywords: pain at the back of the head
weakness in the arms or legs
difficulty moving one side of the body

sections.heading: Types of Stroke
sections.content:
Stroke (cerebrovascular disease) is broadly divided into two types.



■ Cerebral Infarction (Ischemic Stroke)

A condition in which a blood vessel in the brain is blocked by a thrombus (a clot of hardened blood) or an embolus (foreign material carried from another part of the body), so that oxygen and blood cannot reach brain tissue and damage occurs. It accounts for about 80% of strokes.



■ Cerebral Hemorrhage (Hemorrhagic Stroke)

A condition in which a blood vessel in the brain ruptures and bleeding occurs inside the brain. High blood pressure is the main cause, and it can also result from the rupture of a cerebral aneurysm (a balloon-like bulge in the wall of a blood vessel in the brain).



For both types, prompt emergency care is the most important factor in reducing aftereffects.

sections.heading: Precautions for Winter and Seasonal Changes
sections.content:
In winter and during seasonal changes, the risk of cerebrovascular disease increases as temperatures drop sharply, because lower temperatures can constrict blood vessels and raise blood pressure.



■ Prevention Guidelines

- Dress warmly when going out; wearing a warm hat is recommended.

- Minimize the temperature difference between indoors and outdoors.

- Avoid going out suddenly right after waking up in the morning.

- People with high blood pressure, diabetes, or high cholesterol (hyperlipidemia) should not miss doses of their medication.

- Excessive drinking and smoking harm blood vessel health, so limit alcohol and quit smoking.



■ Air Pollution Precautions

Air pollution and seasonal changes are being studied for their relationship to the frequency of stroke. On days when fine dust is severe, wear a mask and limit going outdoors.

sections.heading: Emergency Response to Stroke
sections.content:
The earlier treatment begins after a stroke, the more aftereffects can be reduced. In cerebral infarction, treatment is most effective when started within a few hours after symptoms appear.



■ Symptoms That Require Calling 119 Immediately (FAST)

- F (Face): One side of the face becomes paralyzed or lopsided

- A (Arm): Sudden paralysis or weakness in one arm or leg

- S (Speech): Slurred speech or sudden inability to speak

- T (Time): If any of the above symptoms appear, call 119 (Korea's emergency number) immediately



In addition, if a sudden severe headache, blurred vision, or dizziness occurs, go to the emergency room quickly.



■ Emergency Treatment

- Cerebral infarction: Administration of thrombolytic medication, thrombectomy (a procedure to clear a blocked blood vessel), and other treatments

- Cerebral hemorrhage: Treatment to reduce pressure in the brain and, when necessary, surgical treatment



Treatment of acute stroke requires close collaboration among several departments, such as neurology, neurosurgery, radiology, and rehabilitation medicine.

sections.heading: Prevention and Rehabilitation
sections.content:
■ Managing Risk Factors

The main risk factors for stroke are high blood pressure, diabetes, high cholesterol (hyperlipidemia), atrial fibrillation (an irregular heartbeat), and smoking. Managing these factors consistently can help lower the risk of stroke.



■ Rehabilitation

After a stroke, rehabilitation is important to minimize aftereffects. Speech therapy, motor function rehabilitation, gait training, and other approaches are used to help restore function.



■ Preventing Recurrence

Stroke can recur. Take prescribed medications, such as antithrombotic drugs (medications that prevent blood from clotting), consistently, and have regular follow-up tests.



※ The information in this Health Encyclopedia is for reference purposes only. For accurate diagnosis and treatment, please consult a medical specialist.

records.title: Reflux Esophagitis
records.intro: Reflux esophagitis is a condition in which stomach contents flow back up into the esophagus and cause inflammation of the esophagus. Heartburn and acid regurgitation (a sour fluid rising into the throat) are typical symptoms, and the condition can be managed with lifestyle changes and drug treatment. If symptoms persist, please consult a medical specialist.
records.tags_raw: reflux esophagitis, gastroesophageal reflux, heartburn, acid regurgitation, lower esophageal sphincter, reflux, stomach acid, chest ache, chest pain, chest tightness, feeling of stuffiness in the chest, dry cough, persistent minor cough, cough that will not stop
keywords: feeling of stuffiness in the chest

sections.heading: Causes
sections.content:
There are three main causes of reflux esophagitis.



■ Increased Stomach Contents

When the contents of the stomach increase because of overeating, food staying in the stomach because of reduced gastric motility, excessive stomach acid secretion, and similar factors, reflux occurs more easily.



■ Increased Pressure Inside the Stomach and Abdomen

When the pressure inside the stomach rises because of obesity, pregnancy, or ascites (a buildup of fluid in the abdomen), reflux occurs easily.



■ Reduced Pressure of the Lower Esophageal Sphincter

The lower esophageal sphincter is the muscle that tightens the passage between the stomach and the esophagus. When this muscle weakens, stomach contents can rise more easily. Fatty foods, alcohol, smoking, coffee, chocolate, peppermint, and orange juice can weaken this muscle. Medications such as calcium channel blockers, anticholinergics, and sedatives can also have an effect.

sections.heading: Symptoms
sections.content:
The typical symptoms are heartburn and acid regurgitation.

· Heartburn: A burning feeling that rises from the pit of the stomach (the upper middle abdomen) toward the throat.

· Acid regurgitation: Stomach fluid or food flows back up, leaving a sour or bitter taste.



Other possible symptoms include difficulty swallowing, pain when swallowing, nausea, a feeling that something is stuck in the throat, cough, hoarseness, laryngitis, chronic sinusitis (chronic inflammation of the air spaces beside the nose), and dental cavities. Occasionally, chest pain can be so severe that it is mistaken for angina (chest pain caused by a problem with the blood vessels of the heart). If you have these symptoms, please consult a medical specialist.

sections.heading: Lifestyle Habits
sections.content:
To reduce symptoms, it is important to follow these guidelines.

· Do not overeat, and avoid late-night meals and snacks

· Wait at least 3 to 4 hours after a meal before lying down

· Reduce foods that weaken the lower esophageal sphincter: fatty foods, alcohol, tobacco, coffee, black tea, peppermint, and chocolate

· Reduce foods that directly irritate the esophageal mucosa: sour fruit juices, tomatoes, and carbonated drinks

· Weight loss if you are obese: This can help relieve symptoms.

· If nighttime symptoms are severe: Sleep with the upper body raised



If a medication you are currently taking (such as a calcium channel blocker or a sleeping pill) is making your symptoms worse, do not stop it on your own; please talk with your prescribing doctor to see whether it can be switched to another medication.

sections.heading: Complications
sections.content:
If reflux esophagitis is left untreated, the following complications can develop.

· Chronic cough, laryngitis, sinusitis, and dental cavities

· Esophageal ulcers (sores that form when the mucosa, or lining, of the esophagus wears away) and bleeding

· Esophageal stricture: Repeated ulcers can cause the esophagus to narrow.

· Barrett's esophagus: A condition in which the mucosal cells of the esophagus change after long-term exposure to stomach acid. It is relatively uncommon in Korea, but it is known as a risk factor for esophageal cancer, so caution is needed.



If symptoms persist or worsen, please consult a medical specialist.

records.title: Soft Tissue Sarcoma
records.intro: Soft tissue sarcoma is a malignant tumor (cancer) that arises in the soft tissues of the body, such as muscle, fat, blood vessels, nerves, and connective tissue. It is a very rare cancer, and early detection and treatment are important. If you have a lump on your body that keeps growing over several months, please consult a medical specialist.
records.tags_raw: soft tissue sarcoma, sarcoma, extremity sarcoma, soft tissue tumor, soft tissue neoplasm, rare cancer, malignant tumor, body swelling, facial swelling, leg swelling, swollen hands and feet

sections.heading: Treatment
sections.content:
The main treatment for soft tissue sarcoma is surgery, in which 'wide excision' is performed to remove the tumor together with a wide margin of surrounding normal tissue. This is done to remove even cancer cells that have spread microscopically beyond the visible edge of the tumor.

Sarcomas that develop in the arms or legs can more often be completely removed than sarcomas of the trunk (torso). When there is a large loss of soft tissue after removal, reconstructive surgery (flap surgery) may be performed.

Chemotherapy or radiation therapy may be given before or after surgery, but because there are many different types of sarcoma, the treatment approach differs depending on each patient's condition. For some subtypes, targeted therapies have been developed and are being used.

sections.heading: Definition
sections.content:
Soft tissue sarcoma is a malignant tumor that arises in the soft parts of the body, such as muscle, fat, blood vessels, nerves, tendons, and connective tissue. According to the World Health Organization (WHO) classification, it is divided into more than 60 subtypes. Each subtype is named according to the type of cell and the direction of differentiation (the type of cell it is developing into).

According to a study in Korea, the most common type is undifferentiated sarcoma (about 22.8%), followed by fibroblastic sarcoma (about 21.0%), liposarcoma (about 14.7%), and leiomyosarcoma (about 13.0%).

Soft tissue sarcoma is a rare cancer that accounts for less than about 1% of all cancers, and roughly 1,000 new cases are estimated to occur each year in Korea.

sections.heading: Differences from Benign Tumors
sections.content:
Lumps (tumors) that form in the body are divided into benign and malignant.

· Benign tumors: They grow slowly, do not spread into surrounding tissue, and do not metastasize to other parts of the body. Most are not a major threat to life.

· Malignant tumors (sarcomas): They tend to grow relatively quickly, invade surrounding tissue, and spread (metastasize) to other sites. As a result, they can be a threat to life.

Benign soft tissue tumors can sometimes look like malignant ones, so a diagnosis by a medical specialist is needed for an accurate distinction.

sections.heading: Suspicious Symptoms
sections.content:
In the following cases, sarcoma should be suspected and prompt testing is recommended.

① A lump that keeps growing in size over several weeks to several months

② A lump 5 cm (about the size of an egg) or larger

③ A lump located deep in the body

④ A lump that is painful or tender

Most sarcomas cause no pain in the early stage, so many people leave the lump alone until it becomes very large before seeing a doctor. Unlike benign tumors, malignant tumors are characterized by continued growth. They can also be mistaken for other conditions (such as hematoma, cellulitis, or lipoma), so caution is needed.

sections.heading: Diagnosis
sections.content:
Various tests are performed for an accurate diagnosis of soft tissue sarcoma.

· Imaging tests: MRI (magnetic resonance imaging), CT (computed tomography), and other tests are used to assess the location and size of the tumor and its relationship to surrounding tissue.

· Biopsy (tissue test): A part of the tumor tissue is sampled and examined under a microscope, with immunohistochemical staining, molecular genetic analysis, and other methods to diagnose the exact type.

Because there are many types of sarcoma and diagnosis can be difficult, it is important to be diagnosed at a medical institution that specializes in sarcoma.

sections.heading: Prognosis and the Importance of Early Diagnosis
sections.content:
When there is no metastasis, the 5-year survival rate is reported to be about 70 to 80%. When metastasis has occurred, the prognosis becomes considerably worse. If the diagnosis is delayed because the lump is mistaken for a hematoma that follows an injury, cellulitis, or a lipoma, treatment outcomes may also be worse.

If you have a lump that has kept growing over several months or is 5 cm or larger, please be sure to visit a hospital that specializes in sarcoma and have it examined.

records.title: Frozen Shoulder (Adhesive Capsulitis)
records.intro: Frozen shoulder is a condition in which the joint capsule surrounding the shoulder joint becomes inflamed and the shoulder joint stiffens. Its medical name is 'adhesive capsulitis.' 'Adhesion' means that tissues stick together. If you have shoulder pain, please do not judge the cause on your own; consult a medical specialist.
records.tags_raw: frozen shoulder, adhesive capsulitis, shoulder pain, shoulder stiffness, limited shoulder movement

sections.heading: Definition and Causes
sections.content:
Frozen shoulder is a condition in which inflammation of the joint capsule surrounding the shoulder joint causes the capsule (the pouch that encloses the joint) to stick together, and the lubricating fluid in the joint also decreases. As a result, shoulder movement is severely limited and severe pain occurs.
It mainly occurs in people in their 40s to 70s. It often appears after the age of 50, which is how it got its Korean name, 'osipgyeon' (literally, 'fifty-year shoulder'). However, people who use their arms heavily can develop it at a younger age.

sections.heading: Symptoms
sections.content:
The main symptoms of frozen shoulder are as follows.
· The range of motion of the shoulder is greatly reduced. Movement is limited whether the arm is moved forward, to the side, or backward.
· Pain is especially severe at night and can sometimes make it impossible to sleep.
· Daily activities (such as getting dressed and washing your hair) become difficult.
If you notice these symptoms, it is important to consult a medical specialist promptly. If left untreated, recovery may become more difficult.

sections.heading: Precautions
sections.content:
· Do not assume that any shoulder pain is frozen shoulder. It may have another cause, such as a rotator cuff disorder, and the treatment is different.
· It is important to avoid actions that put sudden strain on the shoulder, such as lifting a heavy object with one hand.
· If you suspect symptoms, do not judge on your own; please consult a medical specialist.

sections.heading: Treatment
sections.content:
Frozen shoulder is commonly said to 'get better on its own if left alone,' but without proper treatment it can become chronic. It is best to treat it actively in the early stage.
· Physical therapy and exercise therapy: The range of motion of the shoulder is increased gradually, within the range that pain allows.
· Injection therapy: Injection into the joint space may be performed at the judgment of a medical specialist.
· Surgery: Surgical treatment is considered when there is no improvement with other treatments.
Please consult a medical specialist before making any decisions about the treatment method and schedule.

records.title: Heat-Related Illness
records.intro: Heat-related illness is an acute emergency condition that occurs after prolonged exposure to a hot environment. It can cause headache, dizziness, muscle cramps, and, in severe cases, decreased consciousness. People who work outdoors, older adults, and children need to take particular care. If symptoms appear, move to a cool place immediately, and if heat stroke is suspected, call 119 (Korea's emergency number) right away. Please consult a medical specialist.
records.tags_raw: heat-related illness, heat stroke, heat exhaustion, heat cramps, heat edema, heat wave, dehydration, summer health, headache, splitting headache, migraine, pain at the back of the head, lack of energy, listlessness, persistent tiredness, body swelling, facial swelling, leg swelling, swollen hands and feet
keywords: pain at the back of the head

sections.heading: Definition
sections.content:
Heat-related illness occurs when the body cannot cool itself enough after being in a hot environment for a long time.
