sections.heading: Panic Disorder and Panic Attacks
sections.content:
A panic attack is a state of intense anxiety that begins suddenly. Physical and psychological symptoms appear together, usually peaking within 10 minutes and subsiding on their own within 20 to 30 minutes.



Typical physical symptoms are as follows:

· Palpitations: a pounding heart or a feeling that the heart is racing

· A feeling of tightness as if unable to breathe, or a sense of choking

· Chest pain or chest discomfort

· Dizziness and lightheadedness

· Cold sweats, trembling of the hands and feet

· A sense of unreality, as if floating

· Numbness or abnormal sensations in the hands and feet

· A feeling of heat rising or of chills



Psychological symptoms include intense fear, such as "I think I'm going to die," "I think I'm going crazy," or "I've lost control."



A panic attack itself can happen once or twice to anyone, for example during a period of extreme stress or after excessive caffeine intake. Panic disorder is a chronic condition in which such attacks occur repeatedly and anticipatory anxiety, worry about "what if another attack comes," interferes with daily life. Because of anticipatory anxiety, people come to avoid public transportation, elevators, and crowded places, which can also lead to social isolation or depressive symptoms.

sections.heading: Causes
sections.content:
Panic disorder is not caused by one specific cause. Multiple factors act together.



· Genetic factors: the risk can be higher if a family member has panic disorder or an anxiety disorder.

· Brain and neurological factors: it is known to be related to overactivation of anxiety-related circuits in the brain or an imbalance of neurotransmitters (chemicals that carry signals in the brain).

· Psychosocial factors: people under extreme stress, with perfectionistic tendencies, or with strong anxious tendencies may be more vulnerable.



It is not a condition caused by weak willpower. It is a mental illness with a biological basis, so professional treatment is needed.

sections.heading: Treatment
sections.content:
Combining medication with cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) may improve symptoms in many patients with panic disorder.



■ Medication

Antidepressants (SSRI and SNRI classes) and anti-anxiety medication (benzodiazepine class) are mainly used. After a period of treatment, the dose can be gradually reduced and stopped in consultation with your specialist. If you suddenly stop your medication on your own because your symptoms have improved, relapse or withdrawal symptoms can occur, so please be sure to consult a medical specialist.



Precautions when taking medication:

· In the early period of treatment, drowsiness, dizziness, and reduced concentration can occur, so avoid driving or operating hazardous machinery.

· Benzodiazepine-class medications in particular can slow reaction time and reduce judgment.

· Drinking alcohol while taking medication can cause dangerous interactions such as excessive sedation, so it should be avoided.

· With some antidepressants, anxiety and restlessness can actually increase during the first 1 to 2 weeks of use. During this period, observation by caregivers or the medical team is important.



■ Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT)

This is a form of psychotherapy that corrects mistaken beliefs about panic attacks and reduces avoidance behavior. It may be more effective when combined with medication.

sections.heading: Lifestyle Management
sections.content:
Improving lifestyle habits along with medication can help control panic disorder more effectively.



· Regular sleep: lack of sleep increases anxiety and the risk of panic attacks. Keep a consistent sleep schedule and a good sleep environment.

· Reduce caffeine and nicotine: they stimulate the sympathetic nervous system, which can raise heart rate and trigger anxiety. Cut back on or avoid coffee, energy drinks, chocolate, and cigarettes.

· Aerobic exercise: do light exercise such as walking or cycling for 30 minutes or more, 3 to 5 times a week. It may help balance neurotransmitters in the brain and ease anxiety.

· Breathing and relaxation training: abdominal breathing, muscle relaxation training, meditation, and yoga can help ease tension and calm yourself during an attack.

· Be careful with alcohol: after a short-term relief of tension, alcohol can cause rebound anxiety and sleep problems, which can worsen symptoms.

· Reduce avoidance behavior: rather than avoiding certain places or situations, gradually exposing yourself under professional guidance and learning how to cope is important for improvement.

records.title: Coronary Artery Disease (Angina and Myocardial Infarction)
records.intro: Coronary artery disease is a condition that occurs when the coronary arteries, which supply blood to the heart, become narrowed or blocked. Angina and myocardial infarction are the main types, and myocardial infarction is an emergency that needs prompt treatment. If you have symptoms such as chest pain, seek immediate medical attention.
records.tags_raw: coronary artery disease, angina, myocardial infarction, coronary angiography, stent, chest pain, heart, collapsing, loss of consciousness, passing out, breathlessness, difficulty breathing, labored breathing, feeling of suffocation, indigestion, bloating, poor digestion, anxious feeling in the chest, restlessness, worrying for no reason

sections.heading: Definition
sections.content:
The coronary arteries are the blood vessels that wrap around the heart like a crown and supply oxygen to the heart muscle. They consist of the left coronary artery (the left anterior descending branch and the left circumflex branch) and the right coronary artery.



When a coronary artery becomes narrowed or blocked, the heart muscle does not get enough oxygen, and the following conditions occur:

· Stable angina: chest pain occurs during exercise or activity and eases after about 5 minutes of rest. It also eases with nitroglycerin (a sublingual tablet).

· Unstable angina: chest pain continues for 20 minutes or longer even at rest and does not ease well even with nitroglycerin.

· Myocardial infarction: a blood clot completely blocks a coronary artery, and the heart muscle dies (necrosis). Prompt treatment is essential.

sections.heading: Symptoms
sections.content:
The most typical symptom of coronary artery disease is chest pain.

· A heavy, pressing feeling on the chest

· A squeezing feeling

· A feeling as if the chest is splitting open



In addition, indigestion, a bloated feeling, dizziness, shortness of breath, and fainting can occur. People with diabetes mellitus may not have clear symptoms.



If chest pain continues for 20 minutes or longer even at rest, or if the pain does not subside even after using nitroglycerin, please go to the emergency room immediately.

sections.heading: Diagnosis
sections.content:
· Coronary CT: a noninvasive test. If no abnormality is found, the result is 98% reliable. If an abnormality is suspected, additional tests are needed.

· Coronary angiography: the most precise diagnostic method. After local anesthesia, a thin tube (catheter) is inserted through an artery in the wrist or groin, contrast dye is injected, and the condition of the blood vessels is imaged directly. It takes about 20 minutes, and diagnosis and treatment (stent placement) can be carried out at the same time.

sections.heading: Treatment
sections.content:
Percutaneous coronary intervention (stent placement) is a procedure that widens a narrowed blood vessel with a wire mesh (stent).

· Stable angina: it can relieve chest pain and improve quality of life.

· Acute coronary syndrome (unstable angina and myocardial infarction): it is an essential procedure that can improve the chance of survival.



For 6 months to 1 year after stent placement, stopping your medication (antithrombotic drugs) on your own greatly raises the risk of recurrence. If an endoscopy, dental treatment, or surgery is planned, be sure to consult a cardiologist before deciding.



For precautions after the procedure (when the wrist is used, 2 to 4 hours of hemostasis is needed; when the groin is used, bed rest is needed), please follow your medical team's instructions.

sections.heading: Precautions
sections.content: After a stent procedure, you take medication that thins the blood. If you stop it on your own, the blood vessel can become blocked again, which is very dangerous. Even for dental treatment or an endoscopy, you must consult a cardiologist first, and you should not make decisions on your own based on information in this encyclopedia.

sections.heading: Prevention
sections.content:
Even after a stent procedure, the following lifestyle changes are important:

· Weight loss: obesity is a risk factor for cardiovascular disease.

· Regular aerobic exercise

· A low-salt diet

· Quitting smoking and alcohol



It is important to manage high blood pressure, diabetes mellitus, and hyperlipidemia well in everyday life and to have regular checkups.

records.title: Holiday Health Care for People with Arthritis
records.intro: During holidays, there are many activities that strain the joints, such as long-distance travel, long hours of cooking, and carrying heavy loads. In addition, arthritis symptoms can worsen in transitional seasons with large daily temperature swings and changes in air pressure. Avoid overexerting yourself with holiday work, and protect your joints with stretching, warm compresses, and appropriate exercise.
records.tags_raw: arthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis (degenerative arthritis), morning stiffness, air pressure, arthralgia, warm compress, cold compress, holiday health, joint protection, joint pain, knee pain, shoulder pain, wrist pain, body swelling, facial swelling, leg swelling, swelling in hands and feet

sections.heading: Weather, Air Pressure Changes, and Joint Pain
sections.content:
The main types of arthritis are rheumatoid arthritis, which is caused by an immune abnormality, and degenerative arthritis (osteoarthritis), which is caused by aging. Both conditions are sensitive to changes in weather and environment.



■ When Air Pressure Drops

When air pressure falls, the balance between the pressure inside the joint and the outside atmospheric pressure is disrupted, and the nerves around the joint can be stimulated. As a result, joint pain can worsen.

- Rheumatoid arthritis: in a low-pressure environment, joint swelling can worsen, and "morning stiffness," in which the joints feel stiff and locked in the morning, can last longer.

- Degenerative arthritis (osteoarthritis): knee and back pain can worsen.



■ When Body Temperature Drops

When body temperature falls, the muscles around the joints contract, so the body feels heavy and stiff, and pain can get worse. If muscles become tense during long-distance driving or carrying heavy loads, blood circulation can decline and pain can worsen. Being exposed to air conditioner or fan air for a long time can cause the muscles and blood vessels around the joints to contract and make pain worse.

sections.heading: Postures and Activities to Watch Out for During Holidays
sections.content:
The areas where arthritis patients most commonly complain of pain during holidays are the knees, back, wrists, and shoulders.



■ Activities That Place a Heavy Load on Women

- Squatting for long periods to trim namul (seasoned vegetables) or fry jeon (savory pancakes)

- Carrying heavy food ingredients

- Standing for long periods to cook



■ Activities That Place a Heavy Load on Men

- Long-distance driving

- Carrying heavy food for ancestral rites



Sitting on the floor for a long time, or repeatedly bending and straightening the knees, can damage joint cartilage (the soft cartilage that protects the ends of the bones). It is important to share roles among family members and avoid overexerting yourself with holiday work.

sections.heading: Lifestyle Guidelines for Protecting Your Joints
sections.content:
■ 1. Regular Stretching

- After waking in the morning, loosen stiff joints with light stretching.

- Stretching for about 10 minutes before and after preparing food can help relieve muscle tension.



■ 2. Light Exercise

When activity decreases during the holiday break, joints become stiffer. Walking or riding an indoor bicycle within a comfortable range is recommended.



■ 3. Using Compresses

- Warm compress: when joints or the back are stiff and painful, it promotes blood circulation and relaxes muscles, which can help relieve pain.

- Cold compress: use it when there is inflammation with joint swelling and a feeling of heat.



■ 4. Managing Your Sleep Environment

Good sleep can help relieve pain. Avoid heavy drinking and irregular sleep patterns, and it is good to take a lukewarm shower or do light stretching before bed.



■ 5. Taking Medication

If the pain is severe, you can take pain relievers or anti-inflammatory medication, but please be sure to consult a medical specialist and take the medication that suits you.



※ The information in this Health Encyclopedia is for reference purposes only. For accurate diagnosis and treatment, please consult a medical specialist.

sections.heading: Managing Indoor Temperature and Posture
sections.content:
■ Indoor Temperature

An environment with appropriate temperature and humidity is good for joint health. After strenuous activity, protect your muscles and joints with a warm compress.



■ Proper Posture

- Avoid staying in the same posture for long periods, and change position or move lightly every 30 to 40 minutes.

- When sitting on the floor, use a cushion to reduce strain on the knees and back.

- When lifting heavy objects, bend your knees instead of bending your back.



■ During Long-Distance Travel

When traveling by car, stop at a rest area every 1 to 2 hours and stretch. Adjust the car seat so that the backrest fits snugly against your lower back.

records.title: Biliary Tract Cancer
records.intro: Biliary tract cancer is a malignant tumor that develops in the bile ducts, through which bile flows, or in the gallbladder. It mainly occurs in people in their 60s and older, and it is often found when jaundice appears after a period without symptoms. The earlier it is detected, the better the outlook for treatment, so if you have risk factors, please have regular checkups.
records.tags_raw: biliary tract cancer, cholangiocarcinoma, gallbladder cancer, jaundice, liver fluke, bile duct stones, painless jaundice

sections.heading: Treatment and Prevention
sections.content:
The most important treatment for biliary tract cancer is surgery to remove the cancer. Surgery for biliary tract cancer is decided according to the location and extent of the cancer. Intrahepatic bile duct cancer is mainly treated with hepatectomy (liver resection), perihilar bile duct cancer with liver resection and bile duct resection, and distal bile duct cancer with pancreaticoduodenectomy. However, biliary tract cancer often has no clear early symptoms and is frequently found at an advanced stage, so whether surgery is possible must be judged carefully through accurate staging.

If surgery is not possible, chemotherapy or radiation therapy is used.

To relieve jaundice, bile drainage may also be performed through endoscopy or other procedures.

At present, there is no officially established screening standard for preventing biliary tract cancer. Reducing risk factors is the best form of prevention.
· Always cook freshwater fish thoroughly before eating it. (To prevent liver fluke infection)
· If you have bile duct stones or a congenital bile duct malformation, receive appropriate treatment.

Please discuss treatment options thoroughly with your doctor.

sections.heading: Definition
sections.content:
Biliary tract cancer is a general term for malignant tumors that develop in the bile ducts, the pathways through which bile (a type of digestive fluid) flows, or in the gallbladder.

It mostly occurs in people in their 60s and older, and the incidence rises with age. It occurs slightly more often in men than in women.

sections.heading: Causes and Risk Factors
sections.content:
The exact cause of biliary tract cancer is not yet fully understood. The following risk factors are known:

· Liver fluke infection: a parasite that can be contracted by eating raw freshwater fish. If left untreated, it can lead to biliary tract cancer.
· Gallstones within the liver
· Congenital bile duct malformations such as choledochal cysts
· Primary sclerosing cholangitis (a condition in which inflammation and fibrosis progress in the bile ducts)
· Ulcerative colitis

Manage known risk factors, and if you have risk factors, please consult a medical specialist.

sections.heading: Symptoms
sections.content:
The most typical symptom of biliary tract cancer is painless jaundice, which appears without pain.

When the flow of bile is blocked by biliary tract cancer, the following symptoms appear:
· The skin and the whites of the eyes turn yellow.
· Urine turns dark brown.
· Stool turns white or gray.
· Itchy skin

Jaundice often appears after the biliary tract cancer has progressed to some extent.

If these symptoms appear, please consult a medical specialist right away.

records.title: Cheilitis (Lip Inflammation)
records.intro: Cheilitis is an inflammatory condition of the lips. Symptoms include cracked lips, flaking skin, or soreness (maceration). Many people do not think of dry, chapped lips as a medical condition, but if symptoms recur or become severe, please consult a dermatologist.
records.tags_raw: cheilitis, lip inflammation, lips, scaling, exfoliative cheilitis, contact cheilitis, actinic cheilitis, angular cheilitis, dryness, winter

sections.heading: Causes
sections.content:
Cheilitis has many different causes.
 · Dry environment: the lips have no pores, so no sweat or sebum is secreted. For that reason, they are easily affected by a dry external environment. It occurs especially often in cold, dry winters.
 · Habit of licking the lips: saliva contains several enzymes, which actually irritate the lips and draw out moisture, making dryness worse.
 · Skin conditions: cheilitis can accompany atopic dermatitis, seborrheic dermatitis, and psoriasis.
 · Contact with irritants: lipstick, lip balm, toothpaste, fragrances, and certain foods (cinnamon, citrus fruits, etc.) can be irritating causes. Nickel and fragrances are the most common culprit substances.
 · Ultraviolet rays: long-term exposure to ultraviolet rays can lead to actinic cheilitis.

sections.heading: Symptoms
sections.content:
Cheilitis appears differently depending on its type.
 · Exfoliative cheilitis: the lips are covered with scales and crusts and peel easily. Cracking, a burning sensation, and pain can accompany it.
 · Contact cheilitis: the lips become itchy and dry, crack, and swell.
 · Actinic cheilitis: it mainly occurs on the lower lip, with flaking and cracking. The border between the skin and the lip becomes unclear. In some cases it can progress to squamous cell carcinoma (a type of skin cancer), so caution is needed.
 · Angular cheilitis: painful soreness (maceration) and cracking appear at both corners of the mouth.
Picking off the flaking skin by hand can actually damage the lips' protective barrier and worsen symptoms.

sections.heading: Treatment
sections.content:
Treatment of cheilitis depends on the type and severity of symptoms.
 · Moisturizing: applying petrolatum (Vaseline) ointment or zinc oxide ointment often can help.
 · Medication: topical tacrolimus, pimecrolimus, or steroid ointment can be used.
 · Contact cheilitis: first stop using the substance that is causing it.
 · When a Candida infection is also present: an antifungal medication is used together.
 · Actinic cheilitis: various methods are available, including cryotherapy, topical treatment, surgical removal, and laser.
If cheilitis is left untreated, complications such as secondary infection can occur. Please be sure to consult a dermatologist.

sections.heading: Prevention
sections.content:
· Correcting the habit of licking the lips or picking at flaking skin is important.
 · In dry seasons, drink water often and apply a moisturizer such as petrolatum to the lips.
 · Keep your oral hygiene clean.
 · Vitamin deficiency can be a cause of cheilitis, so getting an appropriate amount of vitamins may help.
 · Using a lip balm that contains sun-blocking ingredients helps prevent actinic cheilitis.

records.title: Myofascial Pain Syndrome (Muscle Knots)
records.intro: This is the condition commonly described in Korean as getting a "dam," in which a hard, painful lump forms in a muscle or in the membrane (fascia) surrounding the muscle. If left untreated, it can lead to chronic pain, so please be sure to be evaluated and treated by a pain medicine specialist.
records.tags_raw: dam (muscle knot), muscle pain, myofascial pain syndrome, trigger point, injection therapy

sections.heading: Definition
sections.content: Myofascial pain syndrome differs a little from ordinary muscle pain. In a muscle that has become tight, a hard, rice-grain-like band forms, called a trigger point. It is a common condition in which pressing on this spot causes severe pain and pain also spreads to the surrounding area.

sections.heading: Symptoms
sections.content: A deep, stiff, aching pain is felt over a wide area such as the neck, shoulders, back, and lower back. It can hurt even at rest, and pressing on the painful spot causes pain so severe that you may flinch. Sometimes there can be headaches or a tingling feeling in the arms and legs, which can easily be mistaken for another condition, so caution is needed.

sections.heading: Causes
sections.content: It tends to occur when a muscle is suddenly overworked, or when poor posture is held for a long time, such as while looking at a smartphone. It can also appear after a strong impact, such as a car accident, or when mental stress is severe.

sections.heading: Diagnosis
sections.content: It is difficult to detect this condition accurately with machine-based tests such as X-rays or MRI. A doctor makes the diagnosis by listening carefully to the patient's account and feeling the painful area by hand to locate the hard, knotted spot (the trigger point) directly.

sections.heading: Treatment
sections.content: The most widely recognized treatment is a "trigger point injection," in which a needle is inserted directly into the knotted area to release it. Combining this with stretching to lengthen tight muscles, physical therapy, and posture training can help reduce pain substantially.

sections.heading: Precautions
sections.content: When symptoms are mild, they sometimes ease with massage, but handling the area incorrectly can make the pain worse and turn it chronic. If aching pain continues, please do not diagnose yourself from this encyclopedia; be sure to visit a hospital and receive appropriate treatment, such as injection therapy.

records.title: Acute Cerebral Infarction (Ischemic Stroke)
records.intro: Acute cerebral infarction is a very urgent condition in which a blocked blood vessel in the brain damages brain cells. Time is critical, and rapid recognition and emergency treatment are most important, so please seek immediate medical attention.
records.tags_raw: cerebral infarction, acute cerebral infarction, blood clot, thrombectomy, FAST

sections.heading: Symptoms
sections.content: Suddenly, one side of the face droops or becomes crooked, or one arm or leg loses strength and becomes difficult to move. Speech becomes slurred and words cannot be pronounced properly. If these symptoms appear, call 119 right away and go to a major hospital.

sections.heading: Treatment
sections.content: If only a short time has passed since symptoms began, a special injection that dissolves the blood clot (thrombolytic therapy) is given. If more time has passed or the blocked blood vessel is large, a "thrombectomy" is needed, in which a thin tube is inserted directly into the blood vessel of the brain to pull out the clot. Rapid response by an expert medical team is essential.

sections.heading: Precautions
sections.content: If you have "arrhythmia," a condition in which the heart beats irregularly, or an underlying condition that narrows the blood vessels, a cerebral infarction can occur again. Even after leaving the hospital, you need to take your medication faithfully and keep treating the underlying condition.

sections.heading: Definition
sections.content: Cerebral infarction is a condition in which a blood vessel leading to the brain is completely blocked by a blood clot (thrombus), so blood cannot flow. When blood does not flow, brain cells cannot get oxygen and can be permanently damaged.

records.title: Acute Hemorrhagic Conjunctivitis (Apollo Conjunctivitis)
records.intro: Acute hemorrhagic conjunctivitis is a contagious eye infection caused by an enterovirus. It is characterized by bleeding beneath the conjunctiva (the membrane covering the white of the eye), which turns the eye red. It is also called "Apollo conjunctivitis" from the time of the 1969 outbreak.
records.tags_raw: Apollo conjunctivitis, acute hemorrhagic conjunctivitis, enterovirus, subconjunctival hemorrhage, red eyes, contagious, body swelling, facial swelling, leg swelling, swelling in hands and feet

sections.heading: Definition
sections.content: Acute hemorrhagic conjunctivitis is a contagious eye infection caused by an enterovirus (Enterovirus 70). It is characterized by subconjunctival hemorrhage (blood pooling beneath the conjunctiva) that develops rapidly, turning the eye bright red. It first spread in an outbreak in 1969, around the time Apollo 11 landed on the moon, and is therefore also called "Apollo conjunctivitis."

sections.heading: Symptoms
sections.content:
Symptoms appear quickly, within 8 to 48 hours after infection.

· Pain, sensitivity to light, and a foreign body sensation

· Heavy tearing

· Redness and subconjunctival hemorrhage make the eye very red.

· Eyelid swelling



Symptoms last about 5 to 7 days and then improve. Cold-like symptoms can accompany it.

sections.heading: Treatment and Prevention
sections.content:
Because this is a viral illness, there is no specific treatment medication; the goals of treatment are relieving symptoms and preventing secondary infection.

· Antibiotic eye drops are used to prevent secondary bacterial infection.

· Cold compresses reduce swelling and pain.

· Preventing spread: wash your hands often and do not rub your eyes. Do not share personal items with others.



If symptoms appear, please consult an ophthalmologist for diagnosis and treatment.

records.title: Acute Fatigue
records.intro: Fatigue is a state in which the whole body feels weak, or tasks that are usually easy feel exhausting. It is classified as acute if it lasts less than 1 month and chronic if it lasts 3 months or longer. The causes of fatigue are very diverse, so if fatigue lasts 1 to 2 weeks or longer despite enough rest, please consult a medical specialist.
records.tags_raw: fatigue, chronic fatigue, acute fatigue, stress, sleep, anemia, thyroid, lack of energy, listlessness, feeling tired all the time, anxious feeling in the chest, restlessness, worrying for no reason

sections.heading: When to See a Doctor
sections.content:
If fatigue lasts 1 to 2 weeks or longer despite enough rest, please visit a hospital.



Earlier evaluation is needed if any of the following accompany it:

· A fever or heavy night sweats

· Unexplained weight loss

· Energy so extremely low that daily life is difficult

sections.heading: Management and Prevention
sections.content:
The following lifestyle habits can help manage fatigue:

· Regular exercise

· Enough sleep

· Stress relief

· Eating fresh vegetables and fruit



When stress is the cause of fatigue, you may think of it as an insignificant burden, but some people are more sensitive to stress than others. It is best not to conclude on your own judgment alone that stress is not the cause.

sections.heading: Definition
sections.content:
Fatigue is a state in which the whole body feels weak so that daily life is difficult, or in which activities you usually manage well become tiring easily. Reduced memory and concentration and emotional instability are also symptoms of fatigue.



Fatigue is classified by duration as follows:

· Acute fatigue: less than 1 month

· Chronic fatigue: lasting 3 months or longer



Simply feeling overwhelmingly sleepy, short of breath, or having weak muscles are different symptoms from fatigue, but they often appear together with fatigue.

sections.heading: Causes
sections.content:
The causes of fatigue are very diverse.



· Lifestyle factors: stress, lack of sleep, and irregular lifestyle habits are the most common causes of fatigue.

· Mental health: depression can cause chronic fatigue.

· Endocrine diseases: thyroid disease, diabetes mellitus, and others can be causes.

· Infectious diseases: various infections, such as tuberculosis, can be causes.

· Blood disorders: anemia and others can cause fatigue.

· Heart and lung disease, and digestive conditions such as hepatitis, can also be causes.

· Medications you are taking: cold medicine (antihistamines), muscle relaxants, and blood pressure medication can also cause fatigue. If you are taking any medication, please tell your doctor in detail.



If fever, weight loss, or heavy night sweats occur in addition to fatigue, please be sure to consult a medical specialist.

sections.heading: Diagnosis
sections.content:
To find the cause of fatigue, the doctor's interview and examination are most important. It helps to explain in detail, including recent changes in your life, stress, and mental state.



Basic tests include blood tests, urine tests, and imaging tests, and most begin with relatively simple tests.



In about one-third of cases, no particular cause is found even after thorough testing. In this case, the condition is observed for 2 to 4 weeks and then reassessed.

records.title: Orthostatic Hypotension
records.intro: Orthostatic hypotension is a condition in which blood pressure drops sharply when a person suddenly stands up from sitting or lying down, causing dizziness, fainting, and other symptoms. It can also occur in people with high blood pressure. Some studies link it to an increased risk of dementia, so if symptoms recur, please consult a medical specialist.
records.tags_raw: orthostatic hypotension, dizziness, syncope, autonomic nervous system, blood pressure, lightheadedness, headache, a splitting headache, migraine, back-of-head pain, feeling dizzy, spinning sensation, unsteadiness, feeling faint, collapsing, loss of consciousness, passing out, fainting, lack of energy, listlessness, feeling tired all the time

sections.heading: Definition and Causes
sections.content:
Orthostatic hypotension is a condition in which, within 3 minutes of standing up, systolic blood pressure falls by 20 mmHg or more or diastolic blood pressure falls by 10 mmHg or more.



When you stand up, blood pools toward the legs and blood pressure drops momentarily. Normally, the autonomic nervous system detects this and immediately constricts the blood vessels in the legs to maintain blood pressure. Orthostatic hypotension occurs when this autonomic nervous system response does not work properly.



■ Main Causes and Risk Factors

· Autonomic nervous system disorders such as autonomic dysfunction and diabetic autonomic neuropathy

· Older adults (autonomic function weakens)

· Parkinson's disease (a nervous system disease)

· Taking medications that weaken autonomic function

· Situations such as dehydration, bleeding, after meals, after strenuous exercise, and after a sauna

sections.heading: Symptoms
sections.content:
The most common symptom is dizziness, but in severe cases it can lead to fainting.

Other symptoms that can occur include:

· A feeling of vision going dark

· A stiff-necked feeling along with a headache

· Chronic fatigue and a foggy feeling

· Balance problems

· Difficulty breathing if there is a heart problem



■ Orthostatic Hypotension Self-Check

□ Severe dizziness occurs when I stand up after sitting or lying down.

□ My vision temporarily goes dark along with the dizziness.

□ My neck becomes stiff along with a headache.

□ I feel weak all over.

□ The symptoms subside soon after I lie back down.



If half or more of the items above apply to you, consider orthostatic hypotension and please see a medical specialist.

sections.heading: Diagnosis
sections.content:
Diagnosis is confirmed by measuring blood pressure every minute while sitting and after standing. A drop of 20/10 mmHg or more is diagnosed as orthostatic hypotension.

In severe cases, blood pressure and pulse are measured continuously for at least 24 hours, or a head-up tilt table test (a test that measures changes in blood pressure while tilting a special bed) is performed.

sections.heading: Prevention and Lifestyle Management
sections.content:
· Do not stand up suddenly; change position slowly.

· Regular physical activity and balanced nutrition can help.

· Hot saunas, foot baths, and half-body baths can make symptoms worse, so avoid them.

· Staying outdoors for a long time in hot weather can make dizziness worse. If you feel dizzy or unwell, sit or lie down right away.

· Compressing the legs with compression stockings or an elastic band can help limit dilation of the blood vessels in the legs.

· If you have high blood pressure or diabetes mellitus, steady treatment is important for preventing blood vessel and nerve damage.



If symptoms recur or are severe, medication to raise blood pressure may be an option. Please be sure to consult a medical specialist.

records.title: Basal Cell Carcinoma
records.intro: Basal cell carcinoma is the most common skin cancer. It mainly occurs in areas with long-term ultraviolet exposure, and the outlook is generally favorable when it is completely removed by surgery. If you have an area of skin that has not healed for a long time or keeps changing, please be sure to consult a dermatologist.
records.tags_raw: basal cell carcinoma, skin cancer, ultraviolet rays, skin, tumor, mole

sections.heading: Prevention
sections.content: Sun protection is the most important form of prevention. Apply sunscreen daily, and limit outdoor activity during the hours when UV rays are strongest (10 a.m. to 3 p.m.). Wearing a wide-brimmed hat and long sleeves also helps.

sections.heading: Diagnosis and Treatment
sections.content: It is diagnosed by an examination by a dermatologist and a biopsy. The basic treatment is to remove the lesion completely by surgery. The outlook after complete excision tends to be favorable. After surgery, regular follow-up is needed to check for recurrence.

sections.heading: Symptoms
sections.content: At first it can look like a spot (mole) and be overlooked. Over time the lesion grows, and in severe cases it can invade deeply into surrounding tissue. If you have an area of skin that has not healed for a long time or keeps changing, please consult a medical specialist.

sections.heading: Causes and Risk Factors
sections.content: Ultraviolet rays are the most representative risk factor. Intermittent, short, excessive exposure may be more dangerous than long-term occupational exposure to UV rays. It is known to occur more often in people with light skin and light hair. It can develop after a latency period of 20 to 50 years following UV exposure.

sections.heading: Definition
sections.content: This is a malignant tumor (cancer) that develops in the basal layer, the lowest layer of the skin. It is the most common skin cancer worldwide, and also has the highest incidence among skin cancers in Korea. It mainly occurs in people aged 40 and older and is most common in the 60s.

records.title: Pneumothorax
records.intro: Pneumothorax is a condition in which air collects between the lung and the chest cavity (the space inside the chest). The chest cavity is the space that surrounds the lungs. It mainly occurs on one side of the chest, and chest pain and difficulty breathing are the typical symptoms. If you suspect symptoms, please consult a medical specialist.
records.tags_raw: pneumothorax, thoracic pain, dyspnea, lung, air sac, thoracoscopic surgery, recurrence, chest ache, chest pain, chest tightness, feeling of stuffiness in the chest, shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, labored breathing, feeling of suffocation, dry cough, persistent minor cough, cough that will not stop
keywords: feeling of stuffiness in the chest

sections.heading: Definition and Symptoms
sections.content:
Pneumothorax is a condition in which a hole (perforation) forms in the lung and air leaks out and builds up between the lung and the wall of the chest cavity.



The main symptoms are as follows.

· Chest pain: The most common symptom, usually on one side of the chest.

· Difficulty breathing: As the lung is compressed and the condition worsens, breathing becomes harder.

· Persistent cough: Cough can be a symptom of pneumothorax, but conversely, coughing itself can also create a perforation in the lung or make it worse.



If you have chest pain together with respiratory symptoms, please visit a nearby hospital for a chest X-ray.

sections.heading: Causes and Risk Factors
sections.content:
Pneumothorax is divided into two types according to its cause.



■ Primary Pneumothorax

It occurs when air sacs (blebs) form in the lung and rupture. It mainly occurs in teenagers, especially during periods of rapid growth. It occurs more often in tall, thin men, and it has been reported to occur about 6 times more often in men than in women.



■ Secondary Pneumothorax

It occurs because of an underlying lung disease such as pneumonia, asthma, or chronic lung disease. Rather than body type, smoking and the presence of an underlying lung disease are the main risk factors.

sections.heading: Treatment
sections.content:
Surgery is not needed in every case of pneumothorax.



■ Observation

When the pneumothorax is small and symptoms are not severe, the condition is observed.



■ Surgery

Surgery is performed in the following cases.

· Pneumothorax that occurs repeatedly or is highly likely to recur

· Severe difficulty breathing or reduced lung function

· Pneumothorax that may occur on both sides

· Special occupational groups, such as aircraft pilots, public transportation drivers, and divers

· People, such as students preparing for exams, for whom a recurrence would be expected to seriously disrupt daily life



Surgery is performed using a thoracoscope (an endoscope used to view the inside of the chest), and for primary pneumothorax, resection of the air sacs (blebs) is performed through a single incision. The operation takes about 1 hour 30 minutes or less and is a relatively simple procedure.



Please discuss treatment options thoroughly with your doctor.

sections.heading: Postoperative Precautions and Recurrence Prevention
sections.content:
Pneumothorax can recur even after treatment, so caution is needed.



· Smoking cessation: Smoking increases the risk of pneumothorax, so you must quit smoking.

· Avoid sudden exercise: Avoid strenuous exercise during the recovery period.

· Consultation before long flights: Please be sure to consult your doctor before flying.

· Adequate fluid intake: There is no clear direct link between water intake and recurrence of pneumothorax, but adequate fluid intake is good for overall lung health.

records.title: Tension-Type Headache
records.intro: Tension-type headache is a very common headache that is caused not by the nerve tissue of the brain itself but by sustained contraction of the muscles that surround the skull and the back of the neck. Stress, poor posture, and lack of sleep are the main causes. If headaches persist or worsen, please consult a medical specialist.
records.tags_raw: tension-type headache, head pain, forward head posture, posture correction, trigger point injection, rehabilitation therapy, stress, headache, splitting headache, migraine, pain at the back of the head
keywords: pain at the back of the head

sections.heading: Symptoms and Treatment of Tension-Type Headache
sections.content: Drug treatment (such as tricyclic antidepressants) is combined with physical therapy such as low-frequency electrical stimulation. When pain has worsened sharply, trigger point injection therapy is given around the back of the neck and the trapezius muscle, which may help relieve the pain.

sections.heading: Principles and Process of Rehabilitation Pain Treatment
sections.content: The core of rehabilitation treatment for tension-type headache is posture correction, which corrects poor alignment of the cervical and lumbar spine, such as forward head posture. Along with this, muscle relaxants and anti-inflammatory pain relievers, low-frequency electrical therapy, heat therapy, and other methods are applied together to ease excessive muscle contraction.

sections.heading: Relationship to Brain Disease
sections.content: Tension-type headache itself does not indicate a brain disease and is not a direct cause of brain disease. However, if it develops into chronic pain, it can cause cardiovascular and endocrine dysfunction, so appropriate treatment should be received early to keep the pain from becoming chronic.

sections.heading: Causes of Tension-Type Headache
sections.content: It occurs when the muscles of the head and neck contract continuously because of genetic factors, lack of sleep, stress, poor posture, and similar causes. As a result, pain receptors become sensitized and the pain threshold of the central nervous system is lowered, making pain easier to feel.

records.title: Ovarian Cyst
records.intro: An ovarian cyst refers to the various kinds of fluid-filled lumps that form in a woman's ovaries. To protect normal ovarian function, it is important to consult an obstetrics and gynecology specialist carefully and receive treatment.
records.tags_raw: ovarian cyst, teratoma, endometrioma, menstrual pain, robotic surgery

sections.heading: Precautions
sections.content: Surgery to remove the lump can also reduce the function of the normal ovary. A young woman who plans to become pregnant in the future should decide on surgery carefully.

sections.heading: Treatment
sections.content: When surgery is truly necessary, precise robotic surgery may sometimes be used to preserve the remaining normal ovarian tissue with as little damage as possible. In some cases, drug treatment is given first instead of surgery.

sections.heading: Definition
sections.content: It is a condition in which water, sticky fluid, or similar contents fill the ovary, which produces and stores eggs (reproductive cells), forming a pouch-like lump.

sections.heading: Symptoms
sections.content: A teratoma, which contains material such as hair or fat, usually causes no symptoms and is found incidentally. On the other hand, an endometrioma, which forms when menstrual blood collects, can cause severe menstrual pain and pelvic pain and can make it harder to become pregnant.

records.title: Urinary Tract Infection in Men
records.intro: Urinary tract infection is known to be more common in women, but it also occurs frequently in men, and it is increasing, especially in older men along with diabetes and benign prostatic hyperplasia (enlarged prostate). If it is not treated appropriately at an early stage, it can become chronic or lead to sepsis, so prompt diagnosis and treatment are important.
records.tags_raw: urinary tract infection, prostatitis, cystitis, pyelonephritis, urethritis, sepsis, antibiotics, cranberry, sexually transmitted infection, men's health, feeling feverish, body heat, high fever, low-grade fever, body shaking, feeling cold and shivering, cold sensation, frequent urination, going to the bathroom often, hand tremor, body tremor

sections.heading: Types
sections.content:
Simple cystitis is more common in women, but other urinary tract infections, such as prostatitis and pyelonephritis, occur about equally in men and women or more often in men.



The most common form of urinary tract infection in men is prostatitis. Prostatitis refers to any condition in which the prostate becomes inflamed, and it is the most common prostate disease in young and middle-aged men aged 50 and under. It is divided into bacterial and nonbacterial, and acute and chronic types.

sections.heading: Causes
sections.content:
- In their 20s and 30s: Sexually transmitted infection is the most common cause. Your partner must also be tested and treated together.

- Age 40 and older: Prostate-related difficulty urinating, urinary stones, and similar problems are the main causes.

- Older age: Diabetes and benign prostatic hyperplasia (enlarged prostate) often coexist, raising the risk of infection.



Because of population aging, urinary tract infections continue to increase, and together with respiratory infections they can be an important cause of death from infection.

sections.heading: Symptoms
sections.content:
■ Risk of Acute Urinary Retention in Acute Prostatitis

When a man develops a lower urinary tract infection (especially acute prostatitis), he may suddenly be unable to urinate at all, a condition called acute urinary retention. If this state lasts for a long time, kidney function can be damaged, and in severe cases it can lead to death from sepsis.



■ Symptoms That Occur Only in Men

- Penile pain and testicular pain

- Urethritis, orchitis, and epididymitis (inflammation of the tube behind the testicle)



■ General Symptoms of Urinary Tract Infection

Burning pain when urinating, frequent urination (urinary frequency), nighttime urination (nocturia), urgency, pain in the abdomen, groin, or lower back, and fever and chills

sections.heading: Treatment
sections.content:
The most important thing in treating urinary tract infection is to diagnose it quickly and give appropriate antibiotics.



- In the early stage, most cases can be treated without major complications.

- Once it becomes chronic, it is difficult to treat and can cause long-term problems.

- Acute bacterial prostatitis: Antibiotics for at least 14 days, and in severe cases, hospital admission and intravenous antibiotics

- Chronic bacterial prostatitis: Antibiotics for 4 to 12 weeks

- If infections recur repeatedly, the person is checked for congenital abnormalities of the urinary tract.

sections.heading: Prevention and Lifestyle Management
sections.content:
■ Prevention Guidelines

- Keep diabetes under tight control.

- Drink enough fluids.

- If you have difficulty urinating, receive appropriate treatment.

- Do not hold in urine for too long.

- Cranberry is reported to help prevent simple urinary tract infections.



■ Sexually Transmitted Infection

A urinary tract infection caused by a sexually transmitted infection affects not only your own health but also your partner's health. Your partner must also be tested and, when necessary, treated together.



■ Regular Checkups

If you have repeated urinary tract infections, an accurate diagnosis and identification of the cause are needed. Infection can also be associated with various diseases, such as cancer and chronic lifestyle-related diseases, so active management is important.



※ The information in this Health Encyclopedia is for reference purposes only. For accurate diagnosis and treatment, please consult a medical specialist.

records.title: Air-Conditioning Sickness
records.intro: Air-conditioning sickness is a general term for the various physical symptoms that appear when air conditioners or other cooling devices are overused and the temperature difference between indoors and outdoors becomes large. It is not an officially defined medical diagnosis, but headache, fatigue, and digestive problems may occur. In most cases, symptoms may improve within a few days if use of cooling devices is reduced. If symptoms are severe or accompanied by a high fever, please consult a medical specialist.

sections.heading: Definition
sections.content: Air-conditioning sickness (air-conditioning syndrome) refers to the physical symptoms that appear after staying for a long time in an air-conditioned indoor space where the temperature difference between indoors and outdoors is 5 to 8°C or more.

sections.heading: Types
sections.content:
■ Air-Conditioning Sickness Caused by Temperature Differences

When the body cannot adapt to sudden temperature changes, the autonomic nervous system (the nerves that automatically regulate many functions inside the body) is disrupted. As a result, headache, fatigue, digestive problems, and low back pain can occur.



■ Air-Conditioning Sickness Caused by Legionella

Legionella is a bacterium that grows well in warm water at 25 to 42°C. It can multiply in the cooling water of the cooling towers of large buildings and spread through air conditioning. If the bacteria enter the airways, they can cause pneumonia. The risk from household air conditioners is generally considered low.



People more vulnerable to air-conditioning sickness: People with weakened immunity, such as those with chronic heart or lung disease, arthritis patients, older or frail people, and people with diabetes, need to take particular care.

sections.heading: Symptoms
sections.content:
The main symptoms of air-conditioning sickness are as follows.



■ Temperature-Difference Type

· Headache and sleep disturbance

· Fatigue, listlessness, and reduced concentration

· Digestive problems such as constipation, diarrhea, and abdominal pain

· Low back pain and muscle stiffness

· A feeling of swelling in the face, hands, and feet

· In women, menstrual irregularity may also occur.



■ Legionella Infection

In healthy people with normal immunity, the illness often passes like a mild cold. People with chronic illness and older or frail people may develop high fever, chills, and pneumonia symptoms. If high fever and severe difficulty breathing occur, please consult a medical specialist immediately.

sections.heading: Prevention and Management
sections.content:
These are lifestyle guidelines for preventing air-conditioning sickness.



■ Temperature Control

· Keep the temperature difference between indoors and outdoors from exceeding 5°C. The appropriate indoor temperature in summer is 26 to 28°C.

· Adjust the airflow direction so that air from the air conditioner does not blow directly on your body.

· In an air-conditioned room, keep warm by wearing a thin layer of clothing. Change out of sweat-soaked clothes quickly.



■ Ventilation and Cleanliness

· After running the air conditioner for more than 1 hour, ventilate the room for about 30 minutes.

· Clean the air conditioner filter once every 1 to 2 weeks.

· Do not smoke while the air conditioner is running.



■ Fluid Intake

· While cooling is running, indoor humidity can drop to 30 to 40%, drying out the mucous membranes of the airways. Drink warm water or tea often.



■ Lifestyle Habits

· Avoid cold foods and do not overeat.

· Get enough rest and sleep, and it is good to work up a sweat with light exercise once a day.

records.title: Structure and Function of the Brain
records.intro: The brain is the most important organ in the body. It processes all sensory information, regulates bodily functions, and is responsible for mental activities such as memory, thinking, and emotion. It is broadly divided into the cerebrum, cerebellum, and brainstem, and each part has a specific role.
records.tags_raw: brain, cerebrum, cerebellum, brainstem, frontal lobe, hippocampus, neuroplasticity, neuron, dry cough, persistent minor cough, cough that will not stop

sections.heading: The Role of the Brain
sections.content:
The brain is the place where all of the body's information comes together, and it performs the following roles.



· Processes and analyzes sensory information (sight, hearing, touch, and so on).

· Sends movement commands that make the body move.

· Regulates the body's homeostasis (maintenance of a stable internal state), including heartbeat, blood pressure, and body temperature.

· Is responsible for higher-level mental activities such as memory, learning, emotion, language, and thinking.



The brain is firmly protected by the skull, and an adult brain weighs about 1,400 to 1,600 g.

sections.heading: Cerebrum
sections.content:
The cerebrum is the largest part of the brain and consists of four lobes: the frontal, parietal, temporal, and occipital lobes.



· Frontal lobe: Governs higher-level thinking and behavior, such as judgment, planning, concentration, and emotional control. The function of speaking language (Broca's area) is also located here.

· Parietal lobe: Processes bodily sensory information such as touch, pressure, and pain.

· Temporal lobe: Processes auditory information and understands language (Wernicke's area). The hippocampus, which is important for forming memories, and the amygdala, which handles emotional memory, are located here.

· Occipital lobe: Processes visual information. Even if the eyes themselves have normal vision, a problem in the occipital lobe can make it impossible to recognize objects.



The hippocampus plays a key role in forming long-term memory and is one of the first areas to be damaged in Alzheimer's dementia.

sections.heading: Cerebellum and Brainstem
sections.content:
· Cerebellum: Finely controls movement and is responsible for the sense of balance. When there is a problem in the cerebellum, movements such as walking or grasping objects become inaccurate.



· Brainstem: Consists of the midbrain, pons, and medulla oblongata and is located in the deepest part of the brain.

  - Medulla oblongata: Contains the vital centers that control breathing and heartbeat. Reflexes such as coughing and vomiting also take place here.

  - Pons: Relays information between the cerebrum and the cerebellum.

  - Midbrain: Controls eye movement and the pupil response.



Even small damage to the brainstem can be life-threatening. Even when cerebral and cerebellar function has stopped, breathing and heartbeat continue as long as brainstem function is maintained.

sections.heading: Thalamus, Hypothalamus, and Pituitary Gland
sections.content:
· Thalamus: Relays sensory information (sight, hearing, skin sensation, and so on) to the cerebral cortex.

· Hypothalamus: The center that maintains bodily homeostasis, including body temperature, blood pressure, fluid balance, appetite, and sleep. It integrates and regulates the autonomic nervous system and the endocrine system (hormone secretion).

· Pituitary gland: Following commands from the hypothalamus, it secretes various hormones, such as growth hormone and thyroid-stimulating hormone, to regulate the hormone system of the whole body.

· Pineal gland: Secretes melatonin, which is involved in the sleep-wake rhythm.

sections.heading: Key Characteristics of the Brain
sections.content:
The brain constantly needs oxygen and glucose. The brain uses about 20% of the body's total oxygen consumption and about 25% of its nutrients. If oxygen or glucose is lacking, the brain can be damaged quickly.



Brain plasticity (neuroplasticity) is an important characteristic of the brain. It is the brain's ability to reorganize its own network of neural connections in response to brain injury or environmental change. It plays an important role in the recovery of memory and function after brain injury. Consistent learning, exercise, and new activities can help maintain brain plasticity.



The parts of the brain are closely connected to one another, so when one part is damaged, another part can sometimes compensate for some of its function.

records.title: Pneumonia in Older Adults
records.intro: Pneumonia in older adults generally refers to pneumonia that occurs at age 65 or older. Pneumonia is inflammation of the lungs caused by infection with bacteria, viruses, or other organisms. More than 50% of people with pneumonia and more than 90% of people who die of pneumonia are aged 65 or older. In older adults, symptoms are often not obvious, so diagnosis is easily delayed. If you have suspected symptoms, please consult a pulmonology and allergy specialist immediately.

sections.heading: Definition
sections.content:
Pneumonia is a disease in which the lungs become inflamed because of infection with bacteria, viruses, or other organisms. Pneumonia that occurs at age 65 or older is called pneumonia in older adults.



The reasons pneumonia is especially dangerous for older adults are as follows.

· Immune function declines with aging.

· The ability of the airways to clear foreign material decreases.

· Poor nutritional status is common.

· Coexisting conditions are common, such as chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, diabetes, heart failure, kidney failure, and brain disease.

· Cough response and swallowing function decline with aging, which raises the risk of aspiration, in which food or foreign material enters the lungs.

sections.heading: Symptoms
sections.content:
The usual symptoms of pneumonia are fever, chills, cough, sputum, difficulty breathing, and chest pain.



However, in pneumonia in older adults, these symptoms are often not obvious.



· There may be only a low-grade fever without a high fever, or no fever at all.

· Cough and sputum may not be severe.

· It may appear as a sudden lack of energy, reduced appetite, and difficulty with activities.

· In people with dementia, it may appear as a sudden change in mental state.

· Delirium (a state of sudden confusion) may develop and be mistaken for a mental illness.



For this reason, diagnosis can be delayed, which can affect the prognosis. If an older adult lacks energy or seems unusual compared with normal, please visit a hospital promptly.

sections.heading: Treatment
sections.content:
When pneumonia is diagnosed, a decision is made about hospital admission or outpatient treatment depending on the patient's condition. Compared with general adults, older people are admitted to the hospital more often and stay longer.



Treatment uses antibiotics (or antiviral drugs) suited to the causative organism, along with oxygen supplementation and intravenous fluid therapy. With appropriate diagnosis and treatment, the condition may improve, and lasting aftereffects are uncommon. However, the rates of complications and death are higher than in general adults, so active treatment and monitoring are needed.

sections.heading: Prevention
sections.content:
The most important way to prevent pneumonia in older adults is vaccination.



■ Pneumococcal Vaccination

Pneumococcus is the most common causative organism of pneumonia in older adults. People aged 65 or older are eligible for vaccination. A single dose of the 23-valent pneumococcal polysaccharide vaccine (PPSV23) is enough if it is given at age 65 or older; if you received it before age 65, one more dose is recommended at age 65 or older, at least 5 years after the previous dose. If you are unsure about your vaccination history, please consult your doctor.



■ Influenza (Flu) Vaccination

Flu can raise the risk of pneumonia and make symptoms worse. For people aged 65 or older, annual vaccination between September and November is recommended.



■ Other Prevention Guidelines

· Wash your hands often and keep up careful personal hygiene.

· Avoid crowded places when colds or flu are going around.

· Maintain your immunity with balanced nutrition and regular exercise.

· To help prevent aspiration, sit upright when eating and do not lie down right after a meal.

records.title: Glaucoma
records.intro: Glaucoma is a disease in which the optic nerve inside the eye is gradually damaged by high intraocular pressure or other factors, causing the visual field to narrow progressively. There are almost no symptoms in the early stage, so detection can be delayed, and rather than a cure, lifelong consistent management is important. Detecting it early through regular checkups and starting treatment is the best way to help prevent blindness.

sections.heading: Definition
sections.content:
Glaucoma is a condition in which the optic nerve (the bundle of nerve fibers that carries visual signals from the eye to the brain) gradually weakens and the visual field (the range of what you can see) narrows. There are almost no symptoms in the early stage, and in the late stage most of the visual field can no longer be seen and blindness can result, so it is also called the 'silent thief of sight.' Together with macular degeneration, it is one of the leading diseases that cause blindness.



About 4.7% of people aged 40 and older in Korea have glaucoma, making it a relatively common disease. It occurs mainly in older people, but in recent years more cases are being found in people in their 20s and 30s.



Difference from cataract: A cataract is clouding of the lens, which acts like a camera lens, and vision can be restored with surgery. Glaucoma, on the other hand, is a disease in which the optic nerve is damaged, and a nerve that has been damaged cannot be restored with current technology. Therefore, the goal of glaucoma treatment is not a cure but management to keep it from progressing further.

sections.heading: Causes
sections.content:
Glaucoma is a condition in which the optic nerve inside the eye is gradually damaged and the visual field narrows. The most important cause is high intraocular pressure (the pressure inside the eye) that is too high for the optic nerve to withstand.



Intraocular pressure is determined by the balance of aqueous humor (a watery fluid similar to tears) that is produced, circulated, and drained inside the eye. When aqueous humor does not drain well, intraocular pressure rises, which damages the optic nerve.



Glaucoma can develop even when intraocular pressure is within the normal range (10 to 20 mmHg). The most common type of glaucoma in Korea is normal-tension glaucoma, in which intraocular pressure is within the normal range. Because the strength of the optic nerve differs from person to person, at the same intraocular pressure one person may have no problem while another has optic nerve damage.



■ Other Risk Factors

· High myopia (severe nearsightedness)

· Age (40 or older)

· Family history (parents, siblings, children)

· Circulation problems (low blood pressure, migraine, cold hands and feet)

· High blood pressure and diabetes

If you have risk factors, please have regular checkups even if you are young.

sections.heading: Symptoms
sections.content:
Most glaucoma (especially open-angle glaucoma) causes almost no symptoms in the early stage. By the time symptoms appear, the disease has often already progressed considerably.



· Acute angle-closure glaucoma: Intraocular pressure rises suddenly, causing blurred vision, red eyes, and severe pain. In this case, you must go to the emergency room immediately.

· Chronic glaucoma: Reduced contrast sensitivity (difficulty telling light from dark), loss of peripheral vision, and decreased vision develop gradually. The changes differ between the two eyes, and because it progresses slowly, many people do not notice it.



Symptoms can also be divided as follows, according to their cause.



· Direct symptoms of raised intraocular pressure: Red eyes, blurred vision, halos or blurring around lights, and pain in the eye and head

· Symptoms of optic nerve damage: In the early stage there are no particular symptoms other than vague blurring. As the disease progresses, visual field defects appear in which part of the visual field cannot be seen, and in the late stage it can eventually lead to blindness.



Eye strain or eye pain does not necessarily mean that intraocular pressure is high. There may be other causes, such as eye fatigue, dry eye, injury to the surface of the eye, or eye inflammation.



In most cases there are no symptoms until the late stage, so early detection is difficult. If you notice any abnormal symptoms, please consult an ophthalmology specialist immediately.

sections.heading: Diagnosis
sections.content:
Glaucoma is difficult to confirm with a single test; it is diagnosed by an ophthalmology specialist's judgment based on several tests together.



Main detailed tests:

· Stereoscopic optic nerve photography: Checks the structure of the optic nerve.

· Retinal nerve fiber layer imaging

· Optical coherence tomography (OCT, or 'eye CT'): Examines the optic nerve and retina in detail.

· Visual field test: Evaluates the function of the optic nerve.

· Central corneal thickness measurement: Because intraocular pressure can be measured differently from the true value depending on corneal thickness, this is needed for correction.



If a health checkup has given a finding of 'suspected glaucoma,' please consult an ophthalmology specialist for detailed testing. After diagnosis, it is very important to have regular tests to check whether the disease is progressing.

sections.heading: Treatment
sections.content:
The goal of glaucoma treatment is not a cure but slowing progression. Because an optic nerve that has already been damaged does not recover, the key is management to keep it from getting worse.



■ 1. Eye Drops

They lower intraocular pressure, improve blood circulation to the optic nerve, and help protect the optic nerve. There are many types, and the right medication differs from person to person.

· A medication used once a day can be applied at a regular time in the evening. You do not need to go to sleep right away.

· For a medication used twice a day, a 12-hour interval is recommended (for example, 8 a.m. and 8 p.m.).

· Because glaucoma itself cannot be cured, the drops are used continuously.

· Side effects (such as redness, stinging, and pigmentation of the eyelids) can usually be resolved by switching medications. People with asthma or arrhythmia should be sure to tell the doctor in advance.



■ 2. Laser Treatment

It is performed when intraocular pressure is not sufficiently controlled with eye drops alone or when side effects of the eye drops are severe.

· Laser iridotomy: In angle-closure glaucoma, a hole is made in the iris so that aqueous humor can flow.

· Laser trabeculoplasty: Stimulates the drainage outlet for aqueous humor to lower intraocular pressure.

· Trabeculectomy: Surgery that creates a new passage through which aqueous humor (the fluid inside the eye) can drain.

· Glaucoma implant surgery: Surgery that inserts a small tube to create a drainage pathway for aqueous humor.



■ 3. Surgery

It is performed when the condition cannot be controlled with eye drops and laser treatment. The purpose is to lower intraocular pressure, and medication may still be needed after surgery. Surgery does not improve vision and is not a cure. Please discuss treatment options thoroughly with your doctor.



Even after surgery, continued follow-up and management by a specialist are needed.

sections.heading: Prognosis and Lifestyle Habits
sections.content:
The prognosis of glaucoma depends on the type, the condition at the time of diagnosis, and commitment to treatment. Blindness can result when the glaucoma progresses quickly (secondary or angle-closure glaucoma), when it is already severe at the time of first diagnosis, or when treatment is not received properly. Conversely, when it is detected early and managed consistently, the likelihood of blindness can be lower.



Along with regular checkups and treatment, managing everyday lifestyle habits is also important.

· Avoid excessive drinking and smoking.

· Eat dark green and yellow vegetables and fruits that have antioxidant effects.

· Do not drink too many caffeinated drinks.

· Maintain an appropriate weight.

· Avoid exercises in which the head goes below the chest (such as handstands) and exercises that raise abdominal pressure excessively.

· Clothing such as a tie or belt that is too tight can raise intraocular pressure.

· When swimming, wear goggles so that they do not squeeze the eyes too tightly.

· Get regular, sufficient sleep and avoid sleeping face down.

· Using a smartphone for a long time in the dark with the head bowed can raise intraocular pressure, so use it in a proper posture and environment.



If you have been diagnosed with glaucoma, it is important to understand your condition objectively and manage it consistently.

sections.heading: Definition
sections.content: It is a lump (tumor) that grows from the covering of the brain (the meninges). In most cases it is a 'mild' benign tumor that does not spread elsewhere and grows slowly.

sections.heading: Symptoms
sections.content: In the early stage there are no symptoms, so it is often found incidentally during a health checkup. When the tumor grows and presses on the brain, weakness in the arms and legs, slurred speech, dizziness, or decreased vision can occur.

sections.heading: Treatment
sections.content: If the tumor is small and there are no symptoms, it is watched with MRI scans every 6 months to 1 year. If the tumor grows or symptoms appear, surgery to remove it directly or radiosurgery is needed.

sections.heading: Precautions
sections.content: When trying to remove the whole tumor could damage nearby nerves, a safer approach may sometimes be chosen in which part of the tumor is deliberately left behind and radiosurgery is combined to reduce aftereffects (such as paralysis).

records.title: Epilepsy
records.intro: Epilepsy is a condition in which seizures occur repeatedly because of abnormal electrical signals in the brain. In Korean it used to be called 'ganjil,' but the name was changed to 'noejeonjeung' in 2012. Epilepsy is not a single disease but a group of conditions that arise from various causes. If you suspect symptoms, please be sure to consult a neurology specialist.
records.tags_raw: epilepsy, ganjil (former Korean name), convulsion, seizure, antiepileptic drugs, neurology, convulsive seizure

sections.heading: Definition
sections.content:
Epilepsy is a condition in which the brain's electrical signals suddenly become excessively excited, causing repeated seizures. In Korean it used to be called 'ganjil,' but to reduce social stigma about the disease, the name was changed to 'noejeonjeung' in 2012.

Epilepsy is not a disease with a single cause. In childhood, developmental abnormalities or genetic abnormalities are the main causes, and after the age of 60, cerebrovascular disease (a condition in which blood is not supplied well to the brain) or brain tumors are often the cause.

sections.heading: What Symptoms Occur?
sections.content:
Not every shaking movement of the arms and legs is an epileptic seizure. Psychological causes or hyperventilation (breathing too fast) can also cause attacks.

Symptoms differ depending on where in the brain the seizure arises. There may be focal seizures in which only part of the face or limbs shakes, and when the area responsible for language is affected, the seizure may appear as difficulty getting words out.

If you suspect symptoms, please do not judge on your own; be sure to consult a medical specialist for an accurate diagnosis.

sections.heading: Treatment
sections.content:
Epilepsy is a condition that can be controlled with antiepileptic drugs (medications that suppress seizures). With drug treatment alone, 70 to 80% of patients may live without seizures. Each medication has different side effects and each patient responds differently, so a suitable medication is chosen after thorough discussion with the care team.

When seizures cannot be controlled with medication, surgical treatment may be considered. There are operations that remove the part of the brain where seizures arise or block the abnormal flow of electrical activity. Deep brain stimulation (a method of inserting electrodes into a deep part of the brain to stimulate it) and vagus nerve stimulation (a method of stimulating a nerve in the neck) are also used.

Surgical treatment is not possible for every patient, so please discuss treatment options thoroughly with your doctor.

sections.heading: How Common Is It?
sections.content:
Epilepsy newly develops in 30 to 50 people per 100,000, and it is known to affect 4 to 10 out of every 1,000 people. After stroke (a condition in which a blood vessel in the brain becomes blocked or ruptures) and dementia, it is one of the conditions most often seen in neurology.

Some types of epilepsy (status epilepticus, Lennox-Gastaut syndrome, West syndrome, and refractory epilepsy) are eligible for the Special Calculation Exemption program. The Special Calculation Exemption is a National Health Insurance benefit system that reduces the medical cost burden for people with serious diseases.

sections.heading: Precautions
sections.content:
Please keep the following points in mind when taking medication.

The most important thing is to take the medication regularly without missing doses. Stopping antiepileptic drugs on your own because of drinking, taking herbal medicine, taking other medications together, or similar reasons can cause seizures to return and is very dangerous. Even when you are fasting before surgery or endoscopy, you must still take your antiepileptic drugs.

Please be careful, because the following situations can trigger seizures.
- Drinking alcohol
- Lack of sleep
- Severe stress
- Infection (illness of the body caused by bacteria or viruses)
- Uncontrolled diabetes

If you take your medication consistently and have no seizures for 2 to 5 years or longer, a reduction in medication may be considered after consulting your care team. Any change in medication must be made under the guidance of a medical specialist.


In daily life, please keep the following in mind.

■ Driving
According to the guidelines of the Korean Epilepsy Society, driving is possible if you take your medication consistently and have had no seizures for at least 1 year. However, when obtaining or renewing a driver's license, you must self-report and have your fitness to drive determined.

■ Exercise
Exercise can help control epilepsy, so there is no need to restrict it excessively. However, if your seizures are not well controlled, avoid exercise that could be dangerous if a seizure occurred, such as swimming, hiking, and rock climbing.

With appropriate treatment and management, people with epilepsy may be able to lead a social life like anyone else. Please do not miss the time for treatment because of vague fear or prejudice; please consult a neurology specialist.

records.title: Stroke
records.intro:
Stroke is a medical emergency that occurs when a blood vessel in the brain becomes blocked or ruptures. A blocked blood vessel is called a cerebral infarction, and a ruptured one is called a cerebral hemorrhage. If symptoms appear, going to the emergency room immediately is the most important way to reduce aftereffects.



Stroke is also closely related to dementia. The main symptom of stroke is the loss of a specific bodily function, such as paralysis of the arms or legs.



The most important factor in treatment is the golden time (the critical time window for treatment), so please be sure to consult a medical specialist for an accurate diagnosis. If abnormal symptoms appear, call 119 (Korea's emergency number) or go to the emergency room immediately.

sections.heading: Definition
sections.content: Stroke is a condition in which the blood vessels that supply blood to the brain become blocked (cerebral infarction) or rupture (cerebral hemorrhage), damaging brain function. When a stroke occurs, connections in the brain are cut off, and symptoms of 'vascular dementia,' such as a sudden decline in memory or slowed movement, can appear.

sections.heading: Causes
sections.content:
The risk increases with age. Men are affected more often than women when they are younger, and stroke occurs often in winter, when the outside cold narrows blood vessels. If someone in your family has had a stroke, you need to be even more careful because of genetics or lifestyle habits.



High blood pressure is also a main cause, and so is hardening of the blood vessels, the channels through which blood flows, with age. Severe snoring or sleep apnea can lower the oxygen supply to the brain and raise the risk.

sections.heading: Symptoms
sections.content:
Stroke is a condition in which a blood vessel in the brain becomes blocked (cerebral infarction) or ruptures (cerebral hemorrhage). The two look similar from the outside, so they are told apart with a CT or MRI scan.



■ Main Symptoms

· Hemiplegia, in which one arm and leg lose strength

· Facial paralysis, in which one side of the face does not move

· Language impairment, in which speech is slurred or the person cannot get out what they want to say



There are other conditions that cause similar symptoms (such as epilepsy, low blood sugar, brain tumor, and benign paroxysmal positional vertigo), so they must be told apart accurately with brain imaging.



If the symptoms above appear, call 119 or go to the emergency room immediately.

sections.heading: Diagnosis
sections.content:
Stroke is diagnosed through neurological symptoms and brain imaging tests.

· Cerebral hemorrhage: Clearly seen on CT.

· Cerebral infarction: Clearly seen on MRI.



Besides problems with the blood vessels of the brain, a blood clot formed in the heart can travel to the brain and cause a stroke. Therefore, a heart examination must also be done.

sections.heading: Treatment
sections.content:
Stroke is a condition with a golden time.



■ Cerebral Infarction

· For eligible patients, intravenous clot-dissolving medicine is generally given within 4.5 hours of symptom onset. In selected patients, treatment may be considered beyond 4.5 hours, including up to 9 hours, based on advanced brain imaging and specialist assessment. Do not delay seeking emergency care based on the time elapsed.

· In selected patients, a procedure to remove the clot directly is also possible up to 24 hours after the person was last known to be well.

The earlier a patient arrives, the more aftereffects can be reduced, so it is important to go to the emergency room immediately.



■ Cerebral Hemorrhage

Medical treatment or surgical treatment is given. Quick decision-making is important, so you must go to the hospital promptly.

sections.heading: Prevention and Precautions
sections.content:
After a stroke occurs, the cause is analyzed and drug treatment is started. If you stop the medication on your own because your symptoms have improved, the likelihood of recurrence becomes very high. Medication prescribed to match the cause of the stroke must be taken for a long time.



To prevent recurrence, the following risk factors must be managed.

· High blood pressure: Measure blood pressure regularly and control it appropriately.

· High cholesterol (hyperlipidemia): Control blood fats.

· Diabetes: Manage blood sugar appropriately.

· Smoking cessation: Smoking raises the risk of stroke.



Managing risk factors well can help prevent stroke in many cases.

· Regular testing and medication adjustment for high blood pressure, high cholesterol, and diabetes

· Smoking cessation

· Maintaining an appropriate weight through exercise for at least 1 hour every day

· A balanced diet centered on vegetables and fruits

· Caution about excessive outdoor activity in cold weather and on days with severe fine dust



These lifestyle habits also help prevent not only stroke but also cardiovascular disease and peripheral vascular disease.



Please have regular follow-up with your doctor.

sections.heading: Definition and Causes
sections.content:
