Cerebral hemorrhage is a condition in which a blood vessel in the brain ruptures and blood collects inside the brain. Stroke is divided into cerebral infarction (a blocked blood vessel) and cerebral hemorrhage (a ruptured blood vessel). The direction of treatment for the two is exactly opposite. The goal in cerebral hemorrhage is to stop the bleeding, and the goal in cerebral infarction is to open the blocked blood vessel.



The most common cause of cerebral hemorrhage is high blood pressure. If you have high blood pressure, high cholesterol (hyperlipidemia), or diabetes, you must manage them with particular care. People who take antiplatelet or antithrombotic medication should be careful not to take more than the necessary dose.

sections.heading: Symptoms
sections.content:
When cerebral hemorrhage occurs, pressure inside the cranial cavity (the space inside the skull) rises and the nerves of the brain are compressed. Symptoms can include a sudden severe headache, vomiting, decreased consciousness, hemiplegia (paralysis of one side of the body), and language impairment.



Once the brain is damaged, it is difficult to regenerate. In adults, destroyed brain function is hard to recover, so prompt treatment is important.



If abnormal symptoms appear, call 119 (Korea's emergency number) or go to the emergency room immediately.

sections.heading: Treatment
sections.content:
In cerebral hemorrhage, there is no fixed time window called the golden time. If the bleeding requires surgery, it is best to perform the surgery as soon as possible.



Treatment varies depending on the amount and location of the bleeding and the patient's condition.

· Medical treatment: Blood pressure control, treatment of brain swelling, and similar measures

· Surgical treatment: Removal of the hematoma to lower the pressure inside the cranial cavity



The treatment method is determined by your treating specialist. Please be sure to consult a medical specialist.

sections.heading: Prevention
sections.content:
The most important thing in preventing cerebral hemorrhage is blood pressure management.

· Please make a habit of measuring your blood pressure regularly.

· If you have high blood pressure, high cholesterol (hyperlipidemia), or diabetes, please treat them actively.

· If you take antiplatelet or antithrombotic medication, please take exactly the prescribed dose.

· Smoking cessation, moderate drinking, regular exercise, and a balanced diet are good for blood vessel health.

records.title: Hearing Loss
records.intro: Hearing loss refers to a condition in which hearing is reduced and it is hard to hear sounds properly. It has many causes, including aging, noise, and otitis media. According to data from the Health Insurance Review and Assessment Service, the number of patients with hearing loss has been steadily increasing. If you feel your hearing is declining, please do not put it down to age; consult an otolaryngology (ENT) specialist to have the exact cause diagnosed.
records.tags_raw: hearing loss, hearing, hearing aid, cochlear implant, bone conduction hearing aid, auditory rehabilitation, sensorineural hearing loss, conductive hearing loss, ringing in the ears, noise in the ear, cannot hear, difficulty hearing sounds

sections.heading: Definition
sections.content:
Hearing loss is a condition in which it is hard to hear sounds properly. It is divided into three types according to where the problem occurs.



· Conductive hearing loss: A problem in the outer ear (the auricle and ear canal) or the middle ear (the eardrum and the area behind it) prevents sound from being properly transmitted to the inner ear (the cochlea).

· Sensorineural hearing loss: Caused by damage to the cochlea or the auditory nerve (the nerve that carries sound to the brain). Age-related hearing loss (presbycusis) caused by aging is typical.

· Mixed hearing loss: Conductive and sensorineural hearing loss occur together.



Hearing loss is not a condition that affects only older people. It can also occur in young people, including those with congenital external auditory canal atresia (being born with a blocked ear canal), recurrent otitis media, or long-term exposure to noisy environments.

sections.heading: Causes
sections.content: Causes include aging, long-term exposure to loud sounds, inflammation inside the ear, and frequent use of earphones. In recent years it has also become common in young people.

sections.heading: Symptoms
sections.content:
The main symptoms of hearing loss are as follows.



· You often have to ask the other person to repeat themselves during a conversation.

· You have to turn the TV or radio volume higher than before.

· Sounds are especially hard to hear in noisy places.

· Tinnitus (hearing sounds in the ear) sometimes accompanies it.

· The ear feels muffled.



Hearing loss is also associated with withdrawal from relationships, social isolation, and depression. In addition, recent studies have shown a link between hearing loss and cognitive decline (including dementia). If you feel your hearing is declining, please consult a medical specialist.

sections.heading: When to See a Medical Specialist
sections.content:
If you have any of the following symptoms, please consult an otolaryngology (ENT) specialist.



· Sudden loss of hearing

· Difficulty hearing in only one ear

· Tinnitus (ringing in the ears)

· A persistent muffled or full feeling in the ear

· Often having to ask the other person to repeat themselves during a conversation



Many people recognize the importance of hearing only after it has been lost. The earlier hearing loss is diagnosed and appropriate treatment is started, the better auditory rehabilitation tends to work.

sections.heading: Treatment
sections.content:
Treatment of hearing loss depends on the type and degree.



■ Hearing Aids

This is the first auditory rehabilitation method considered once hearing loss is diagnosed. It amplifies sound and delivers it to the inner ear through the eardrum and middle ear. However, its effect is limited in external auditory canal atresia (a blocked ear canal), recurrent otitis media, and severe hearing loss.



■ Cochlear Implant

It is considered for patients with severe sensorineural hearing loss who cannot get adequate benefit from hearing aids. It is a device in which electrodes are inserted into the cochlea to deliver sound signals directly to the auditory nerve.



■ Bone Conduction Hearing Aid Implantation

This method delivers sound to the cochlea through vibration of the bone (the skull). It is suitable for patients who cannot use a standard hearing aid because of a problem in the ear canal or middle ear. Recently, implantable devices in which a small device is placed under the skin have been developed and applied in clinical practice.



The treatment method is determined by a specialist according to the patient's condition and type of hearing loss. Please be sure to consult an otolaryngology (ENT) specialist thoroughly.

sections.heading: Prevention
sections.content: It is best to keep earphone volume at 60% or lower and to use earphones for no more than 60 minutes a day. In noisy places, wear earplugs, and after hearing a loud sound, give your ears a rest in a quiet place.

records.title: Hearing Loss and Bone Conduction Hearing Aid Implantation
records.intro: Hearing loss is not just a symptom of difficulty hearing sounds; it affects overall quality of life, including withdrawal from relationships, depression, and cognitive decline. In recent years, bone conduction hearing aid implantation, which delivers sound through the bone, has been used for patients who have difficulty using conventional hearing aids. If your hearing declines, please do not leave it untreated by blaming 'age'; consult a medical specialist.
records.tags_raw: hearing loss, sensorineural hearing loss, conductive hearing loss, hearing aid, bone conduction hearing aid, cochlear implant, presbycusis, otitis media, external auditory canal atresia, dementia, cognitive decline, cannot hear, difficulty hearing sounds

sections.heading: Types
sections.content:
Hearing loss refers to a reduced ability to hear sounds, and it is classified as follows according to whether the problem is that sound does not reach the cochlea (inner ear) or that the cochlea or auditory nerve itself is damaged.



- Conductive hearing loss: A problem in the outer ear (from the auricle to the eardrum) or the middle ear (between the eardrum and the cochlea) prevents sound from reaching the inner ear. Causes include congenital external auditory canal atresia and recurrent otitis media.



- Sensorineural hearing loss: Caused by damage to the cochlea or auditory nerve. Age-related hearing loss (presbycusis) is the most common cause, and noise exposure and medication side effects can also be causes.



- Mixed hearing loss: Both types occur together.



Chronic sensorineural hearing loss is difficult to recover with medication or surgery, so assistive devices such as hearing aids or cochlear implants are needed.

sections.heading: Hearing Aids and Their Limitations
sections.content:
Once hearing loss is diagnosed, wearing a hearing aid is considered first. However, hearing aids are not effective for every patient.



■ Cases in Which It Is Difficult to Wear a Standard Hearing Aid

- The external auditory canal (ear canal) is blocked from birth

- Discharge and inflammation are frequent because of recurrent otitis media

- The external auditory canal is so deformed that a hearing aid cannot be worn

- Hearing loss is so severe that a hearing aid has little effect



In the past, people in these situations had no choice but to put up with difficulty communicating, but recently a new alternative, bone conduction hearing aid implantation, has been attracting attention.

sections.heading: Bone Conduction Hearing Aid Implantation
sections.content:
■ What Is a Bone Conduction Hearing Aid?

A standard hearing aid amplifies sound and delivers it to the inner ear through the eardrum and middle ear. A bone conduction hearing aid, on the other hand, directly vibrates the bone of the skull so that the cochlea perceives the sound. It is especially effective for patients who have a problem in the ear canal or middle ear.



■ Implantable Bone Conduction Hearing Aid

In this method, a small device is placed under the skin and connected to an external sound processor to deliver sound. While minimizing skin damage and hygiene problems, it can provide a clearer and more stable listening environment.



■ Who It Applies To

It is used for patients who have difficulty using conventional hearing aids, such as those with conductive hearing loss, mixed hearing loss, congenital external ear canal malformation, or chronic otitis media. Whether it is suitable should be decided through consultation with a medical specialist.

sections.heading: Hearing Loss, Dementia, and Cognitive Function
sections.content:
Several recent studies have shown a link between hearing loss and dementia or cognitive decline. Some study results indicate that the greater the hearing loss, the higher the risk of cognitive decline and dementia. One explanation is that social isolation and reduced communication caused by hearing loss decrease stimulation of the brain.



■ Prevention and Management

- If you feel your hearing is declining, do not leave it untreated by blaming age; please consult a medical specialist for an accurate diagnosis.

- Actively use treatment and assistive devices suited to your situation, such as hearing aids, cochlear implants, and bone conduction hearing aid implantation.

- In very noisy environments, wear earplugs or hearing protection.

- When using ototoxic drugs (medications that can damage the cochlea), tell your doctor and take care.



Hearing has a very large effect on quality of life and overall health, so early diagnosis and active rehabilitation are important.



※ The information in this Health Encyclopedia is for reference purposes only. For accurate diagnosis and treatment, please consult a medical specialist.

records.title: Urinary Incontinence in Men
records.intro: Urinary incontinence does not occur only in women; it also occurs in men, and the number of men with urinary incontinence is increasing with population aging and a rise in prostate disease. It often occurs after prostate surgery or because of benign prostatic hyperplasia (enlarged prostate), diabetes, and similar conditions. It can be managed with proper care, including Kegel exercises, drug treatment, and, when necessary, surgical treatment, so please consult a medical specialist.
records.tags_raw: urinary incontinence, male urinary incontinence, stress urinary incontinence, urge urinary incontinence, prostate surgery, Kegel exercises, artificial urinary sphincter, urinary frequency, overactive bladder, dry cough, persistent minor cough, cough that will not stop, frequent urination, going to the bathroom often

sections.heading: Definition
sections.content: Urinary incontinence is a condition in which urine leaks regardless of a person's will. It tends to occur as the function of the nerves that control the bladder muscle and the sphincter declines with age.

sections.heading: Causes
sections.content:
- After prostate surgery (especially radical prostatectomy for prostate cancer)

- Benign prostatic hyperplasia (enlarged prostate)

- Underlying conditions such as diabetes and Parkinson's disease

- Overactive bladder

sections.heading: Types
sections.content:
- Stress incontinence: Urine leaks when abdominal pressure increases, such as with coughing or bending

- Urge incontinence: A sudden, urgent need to urinate causes leakage before reaching the bathroom

- Mixed incontinence: Both types occur together

- Overflow incontinence: The bladder becomes so full of urine that it overflows and leaks (when bladder function is impaired)

sections.heading: Diagnosis
sections.content: A symptom questionnaire, prostate ultrasound, and urodynamic testing (a detailed evaluation of bladder function) are performed.

sections.heading: Treatment
sections.content:
■ Behavioral Therapy (First-Line Treatment)

- Kegel exercises (anal sphincter-tightening exercises): Strengthen the sphincter and pelvic muscles. Repeatedly tighten and release the anus. They are essential for recovery from incontinence after prostate surgery.

- Lifestyle changes: Reduce spicy foods, acidic foods, and caffeine.



■ Drug Treatment

- Urge incontinence: Medications that reduce bladder overactivity are used.

- Combining Kegel exercises with drug treatment may give good results.



■ Surgical Treatment

When recovery does not occur after a certain period following radical prostatectomy, artificial urinary sphincter implantation (surgery that inserts a device that tightens the urethra) may be considered.



In most cases, incontinence after prostate surgery may improve over time. Doing Kegel exercises consistently is the most important thing.

sections.heading: Regular Checkups
sections.content:
■ Recommended Prostate Screening Guidelines

The condition of the prostate is checked with a prostate-specific antigen (PSA) blood test.

- Age 45 and older: Starting PSA testing is recommended.

- Ages 55 to 69: PSA testing at intervals of 2 years or longer is recommended.

- If PSA is above 3 ng/mL, or if there is an abnormal finding on the examination in which the prostate is felt through the anus (digital rectal examination), further testing is needed.

- People at high risk because of a family history are advised to start screening at an earlier age.



※ The information in this Health Encyclopedia is for reference purposes only. For accurate diagnosis and treatment, please consult a medical specialist.

records.title: Cold and Hot Compresses
records.intro: Compresses are often used to relieve pain and loosen stiff joints. However, hot or cold compresses must be chosen appropriately depending on when the injury occurred and the person's condition, so it is safer to follow a medical specialist's diagnosis than to decide on your own.
records.tags_raw: hot compress, cold compress, arthritis, muscle pain, hot and cold therapy, paraffin bath, ice pack, body swelling, facial swelling, leg swelling, swollen hands and feet

sections.heading: How to Use Hot Compresses and Precautions
sections.content:
■ How to Use a Hot Compress

Electric heating pads, electric compress devices, infrared heat (useful when the skin needs to be observed), paraffin baths (effective for the joints of the hands and feet), foot baths, and similar devices are used.



■ Precautions - When Not to Use a Hot Compress

· Immediately after an acute injury or inflammation

· When there is trauma or bleeding

· Areas with reduced sensation

· Unconscious patients

· When there are wounds or scars on the skin

· Over the uterus of a pregnant woman

sections.heading: Definition
sections.content: A hot compress widens blood vessels so that blood flows well and loosens stiff muscles and joints. A cold compress, on the other hand, narrows blood vessels, which can reduce swelling, calm inflammation, and make pain feel less intense.

sections.heading: Choosing Between the Two
sections.content:
■ Which Is Better, a Hot Compress or a Cold Compress?

If an acute injury, or an acute or subacute condition, is suspected, a cold compress is safer. A hot compress can help with chronic pain or before joint exercise. Please discuss specific usage with your doctor or therapist.

sections.heading: Effects of Hot Compresses
sections.content:
■ Effects of Hot Compresses (Heat Therapy)

· Increased elasticity (flexibility) of connective tissue

· Relief of joint stiffness

· Pain relief

· Reduced muscle spasm

· Increased blood flow

· Faster absorption of inflammatory byproducts, edema, and exudate



■ When Hot Compresses Can Help

Chronic pain, muscle spasm, joint contracture (stiffening of a joint), chronic bursitis (chronic inflammation of the fluid-filled sac around a joint), tenosynovitis (inflammation of the sheath around a tendon), and similar conditions

sections.heading: How to Use Cold Compresses and Precautions
sections.content:
■ How to Use a Cold Compress

Wrap ice pieces or an ice pack in a towel before using it. Take care not to let it touch the skin directly.



■ Precautions - When Not to Use a Cold Compress

· Cold allergy

· Raynaud's syndrome (a condition in which the fingers and toes are sensitive to cold)

· Cardiovascular insufficiency

· Unconscious patients

sections.heading: Effects of Cold Compresses
sections.content:
■ Effects of Cold Compresses (Cold Therapy)

· Reduced metabolic activity in the body

· Reduced blood flow

· Reduced muscle tension

· Suppression of spasm

· Pain relief

· Reduced joint inflammation



■ When Cold Compresses Can Help

Immediately after acute trauma or injury, pain, arthritis, and muscle spasm

records.title: Norovirus Infection
records.intro: Norovirus infection is acute gastroenteritis caused by norovirus. It circulates mainly in winter (November to February) and spreads through contaminated food or water and through contact between people. Hygiene practices such as handwashing are the most important way to prevent it, and most people recover on their own.
records.tags_raw: norovirus, food poisoning, winter food poisoning, acute gastroenteritis, diarrhea, vomiting, handwashing, stomachache, tummy ache, bellyache, pain inside the abdomen, feeling feverish, body heat, high fever, low-grade fever, lack of energy, listlessness, persistent tiredness, loose stools, watery diarrhea, frequent bathroom visits

sections.heading: Definition
sections.content: Norovirus infection is acute gastroenteritis (inflammation of the stomach and intestines) caused by norovirus. It is one of the common causes of 'food poisoning' and circulates mainly in winter (November to February).

sections.heading: Causes
sections.content:
The routes of transmission are as follows.

· Eating contaminated food (especially shellfish such as oysters, and uncooked vegetables)

· Drinking contaminated water

· Direct contact with an infected person

· Tiny droplets released from the vomit of an infected person



Symptoms appear 10 to 48 hours after exposure.

sections.heading: Symptoms
sections.content:
The main symptoms are as follows.

· Nausea and vomiting

· Diarrhea

· Abdominal pain

· Whole-body symptoms such as fever, muscle pain, and fatigue may accompany them.



Gastrointestinal symptoms usually last 24 to 48 hours, and most people recover on their own.

sections.heading: Treatment
sections.content:
There is currently no specific treatment drug or vaccine for norovirus infection.



The most important treatment is replacing enough fluids to prevent dehydration. Drink plenty of water, barley tea, electrolyte drinks, and similar fluids.



If symptoms are severe or recovery is slow, please consult a medical specialist.

sections.heading: Prevention
sections.content:
The following methods can help prevent norovirus infection.



· Handwashing: Wash with soap under running water for at least 30 seconds. Be sure to wash after going outside, after using the bathroom, and before meals.

· Cook food thoroughly at 85°C for at least 1 minute before eating. In particular, always cook oysters and other shellfish before eating.

· Wash vegetables thoroughly before eating.

· Drink boiled water or packaged beverages.

· People who have been infected should limit group activities for 24 to 72 hours after symptoms disappear.

· Disinfect an infected person's vomit and the items they have touched with a chlorine-based disinfectant.



Even in winter, it is important not to let your guard down in preventing food poisoning.

records.title: Presbyopia
records.intro: Presbyopia is a condition in which the lens inside the eye loses elasticity with age, making it hard to see things up close. It is a natural part of aging that begins to appear in the early to mid 40s. If you have troublesome symptoms, please consult an ophthalmology specialist.
records.tags_raw: presbyopia, lens, reading glasses, accommodation, near vision, multifocal lenses, presbyopia surgery, headache, splitting headache, migraine, pain at the back of the head
keywords: pain at the back of the head

sections.heading: Definition
sections.content:
When looking at a nearby object, the lens inside the eye (which acts like a camera lens) changes shape to increase its focusing power. This is called 'accommodation.' Presbyopia is a condition in which the lens hardens and loses elasticity with age, so this ability to accommodate declines.



It is a natural part of aging and mainly appears in the early to mid 40s. People who are farsighted may notice it earlier, and people who are nearsighted may notice it later because taking off their glasses compensates for it to some extent.

sections.heading: Symptoms
sections.content:
· Text at a close distance, such as in books and on smartphones, looks blurry and has to be held farther away to be seen.

· Headache occurs after looking at close objects for a long time.

· It is harder to see close objects in dim light.

sections.heading: Treatment
sections.content:
The basic treatment for presbyopia is prescription glasses. After a refraction test, glasses that suit the condition of the eyes are prescribed.

· People who did not usually wear glasses: Reading glasses for near vision

· People who wore nearsighted glasses: Near-vision glasses with a lower prescription, or multifocal glasses



'Presbyopia surgery' is a method that addresses presbyopia and cataract together by inserting a multifocal intraocular lens during cataract surgery. If surgery is rushed because of presbyopia when the cataract is not severe, side effects can actually occur. Please decide on surgery carefully, and receive basic treatment such as glasses first. Please discuss treatment options thoroughly with your doctor before deciding.

sections.heading: Management
sections.content: No method is currently known to prevent presbyopia or slow its progression. Presbyopia is a natural part of aging, and wearing glasses that suit the condition of the eyes is the basic approach. It is important to check, with an eye examination once every 6 months to 1 year, that other eye diseases such as cataract and glaucoma are not present.

records.title: Itchy Skin in Older Adults (Senile Pruritus)
records.intro: Itchy skin in older adults is a common symptom in people in their 60s and older, and dry skin is the main cause. If the itching persists or becomes so severe that it disturbs sleep, please consult a dermatology specialist.
records.tags_raw: itchy skin, aging skin, dry skin (xerosis), itching, winter, moisturizing, eczema craquelé (cracked eczema)

sections.heading: Treatment
sections.content:
· Apply moisturizer generously at least twice a day. Applying it right after bathing is effective.
 · If symptoms are severe, treatment with antihistamines and steroid lotion for 1 to 2 weeks may relieve them.

If there is no response to treatment, or if the itching is so severe that it disturbs sleep, another skin disease or a systemic disease may be the cause, so please be sure to consult a medical specialist.

sections.heading: Precautions
sections.content:
· Do not make the bath water too hot.

· Do not scrub the skin to remove dead skin (body scrubbing). Even if it is a long-standing habit, it must be corrected when there is itching or dry skin.

 · Finish showers within 10 minutes.

sections.heading: Causes
sections.content:
The most common cause of itchy skin in older adults is dry skin. When lipids (oily substances) on the skin surface become insufficient, water escapes into the air and the skin dries out.
 · With age, the sebum secretion that helps the skin retain moisture decreases.
 · Often there are no symptoms in spring and summer, and symptoms worsen in autumn and winter.
 · Symptoms worsen when the bath water is too hot, when the skin is scrubbed, or when showers are long.
 · The winter environment, with high indoor temperatures and low humidity, also worsens symptoms.

sections.heading: Symptoms
sections.content:
· Severe itching mainly occurs on the arms and legs. It does not often occur on the face, scalp, or the palms and soles.
 · The skin surface becomes rough, and white flakes appear.
 · In severe cases, the skin cracks and can progress to eczema craquelé (cracked eczema), in which fine cracks form like those in old porcelain.
 · It is very common in older people, occurring in more than 50% of people aged 70 and older.

records.title: Multiple Myeloma
records.intro: Multiple myeloma is a blood cancer in which cancer develops in plasma cells (the cells that make antibodies). It mainly occurs in older adults. Anemia, kidney failure, bone pain, and repeated fractures are characteristic symptoms. If you develop bone pain, repeated fractures of unknown cause, or anemia, please consult a hematology-oncology specialist.
records.tags_raw: multiple myeloma, blood cancer, plasma cell, fracture, vertebral fracture, bone pain, kidney failure, monoclonal antibody, lack of energy, listlessness, persistent tiredness, body swelling, facial swelling, leg swelling, swollen hands and feet, nausea, feeling about to vomit, vomiting, unable to pass stool, difficulty having a bowel movement, hard stools

sections.heading: What Is Multiple Myeloma?
sections.content:
Multiple myeloma is a blood cancer in which cancer develops in plasma cells, the cells that make antibodies (immune proteins). Plasma cells are a type of white blood cell.



The cancerous plasma cells produce large amounts of an abnormal antibody (a monoclonal antibody). This antibody cannot perform its normal function, so the patient's immunity actually decreases. It can also damage the kidneys and cause kidney failure (reduced kidney function).



It is a blood cancer that mainly occurs in older adults.

sections.heading: Symptoms
sections.content:
The main symptoms of multiple myeloma are as follows.



· Bone pain: Cancer cells weaken the bones, causing severe bone pain. Pain in the lower back and back is especially common.

· Fractures: The bones weaken, making fractures such as spinal compression fractures more likely.

· Anemia: Fatigue, paleness, and dizziness occur.

· Weakened immunity: Repeated infections are more likely.

· Kidney failure: Reduced kidney function can cause decreased urine output, swelling (edema), and similar problems.

· Hypercalcemia (an abnormally high calcium level in the blood): Nausea, vomiting, constipation, and listlessness can occur.



A characteristic finding is a high protein level on blood tests.

sections.heading: Diagnosis and Treatment
sections.content:
For diagnosis, blood tests, urine tests, bone marrow tests, and imaging tests (X-ray, CT, MRI, and others) are performed.



Treatment is determined by the patient's age, overall health, and the stage of the disease.



· In some cases, the condition is monitored without immediate treatment.

· When treatment becomes necessary, chemotherapy is given using a combination of injectable or oral chemotherapy drugs.

· When appropriate, hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (mainly autologous transplantation) is considered.



Please discuss the treatment method and plan thoroughly with a hematology-oncology specialist before deciding.

records.title: Gallbladder Cancer
records.intro: The gallbladder is a small pouch that temporarily stores the digestive fluid (bile) made in the liver. Gallbladder cancer, a malignant tumor that develops there, causes no obvious symptoms until the disease is quite advanced, which makes early detection very difficult. If you have persistent indigestion or abdominal pain, please do not dismiss it on your own; be sure to consult a medical specialist for an examination and detailed tests.
records.tags_raw: gallbladder cancer, bile duct cancer, gallbladder, gallstones, cholecystitis, abdominal ultrasound, jaundice, laparoscopy, stomachache, tummy ache, bellyache, pain inside the abdomen, feeling of indigestion (food stuck), bloated feeling in the stomach, poor digestion

sections.heading: Symptoms
sections.content:
In the early stage, gallbladder cancer usually causes no symptoms at all, or its symptoms resemble those of a mild stomach ailment, so it is very hard to notice.



· Early symptoms: Digestion after meals is worse than usual, or there is mild abdominal pain. Weight may also drop for no particular reason.

· Symptoms as the disease progresses: When the cancer grows and completely blocks the passage through which digestive fluid flows, very severe pain in the upper right abdomen or fever can occur.

· Symptoms when it worsens: When the disease has progressed considerably, 'jaundice,' in which the whites of the eyes and the skin turn yellow, appears. A hard lump may also be felt by hand in the upper right abdomen.



By the time symptoms are noticed and a hospital is visited, the cancer has often already spread to other areas.

sections.heading: Causes
sections.content:
The clear, direct cause of gallbladder cancer has not yet been fully identified, but gallstones, the hard stones that form inside the gallbladder, are known to be closely related to the development of cancer.



· Effect of gallstones: When gallstones continually scrape and irritate the inner wall of the gallbladder over a long period and cause inflammation, the nature of the cells can change and progress to cancer.

· Age and conditions: Cancer is often found in people with 'chronic cholecystitis,' in which the gallbladder wall thickens and no longer functions properly. Older patients, mainly in their 60s and older, account for 85% of all cases, but it also occurs in younger people not infrequently, so being young does not mean you are not at risk.

sections.heading: Diagnosis
sections.content:
The quickest and easiest way to look inside the body for early diagnosis is an 'abdominal ultrasound.'

Even without symptoms, more and more cases are being found early by chance during an abdominal ultrasound in the national health checkup or a private comprehensive checkup.



If an ultrasound finds an abnormally large lump (lesion) of 1 cm or more in the gallbladder, or if cancer is suspected, further detailed tests such as computed tomography (CT) or magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) must be done to check thoroughly how far the cancer has spread, such as to the lymph nodes or the liver.

sections.heading: Treatment
sections.content:
To date, the most basic and important medical treatment for gallbladder cancer is to remove the tumor surgically.



· Extent of surgery: If the cancer remains only on the surface of the mucosa (the shallow layer), it is enough to remove just the affected gallbladder. However, if the cancer has penetrated deep into the tissue, a wide resection is needed that removes not only the gallbladder but also a portion of the surrounding liver and nearby organs such as the lymph nodes, to be safe.

· Surgical method: In the past, open surgery, with a large incision of about 15 to 20 cm on the right side of the abdomen, was mainly used. In recent years, with advances in medical technology, laparoscopic surgery, which makes only small openings of 1 to 2 cm in the abdomen, and precise robotic surgery have been widely performed, which can greatly reduce scarring and pain.

sections.heading: Prevention and Precautions
sections.content:
Around the gallbladder, the liver, duodenum, colon, and large blood vessels are tightly intertwined. For this reason, even a small spread of gallbladder cancer to the surrounding area makes surgery extremely difficult.



In fact, when the cancer is found very early, before stage 1 while it is still confined to the mucosa, the survival rate exceeds 90%, but by stage 2 the survival rate falls to half or less.



Therefore, getting an abdominal ultrasound carefully at health checkups to detect the cancer early is the most important measure against gallbladder cancer. If your doctor recommends surgery for gallstones or chronic cholecystitis, it is recommended not to put off treatment and to have the surgery on time.

records.title: Pituitary Tumor
records.intro: A pituitary tumor is a tumor that develops in the pituitary gland, a small organ in the middle of the brain. Most are benign tumors and are not cancer. As the tumor grows or hormone secretion is disrupted, various symptoms can appear, so if you have suspected symptoms, please consult a medical specialist.
records.tags_raw: pituitary gland, pituitary tumor, pituitary adenoma, decreased vision, visual field defect, acromegaly, Cushing's syndrome, amenorrhea, brain tumor, blurry vision, difficulty seeing, hazy vision, seeing double, overlapping images

sections.heading: Definition
sections.content:
The pituitary gland is a small organ, about 1 cm in size, located in the middle of the head. It receives signals from the hypothalamus (the part of the brain that regulates bodily functions) and secretes the various hormones the body needs. Hormones are chemical signals that regulate the function of each organ in the body.

A pituitary tumor, that is, a pituitary adenoma, is a tumor that develops in this gland. Most are benign tumors, which differ from cancers that spread to surrounding areas. In Korea, about 2,000 people are diagnosed each year, and it is the second most common type of brain tumor.

Pituitary tumors are broadly divided into two types.

· Functioning adenoma: A tumor that secretes hormones in excess. Examples include prolactin-, growth hormone-, and adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH)-secreting adenomas.

· Nonfunctioning adenoma: A tumor that does not secrete hormones in excess.

sections.heading: Symptoms
sections.content:
The pituitary gland sits just below the optic nerve (the nerve that connects the eye and the brain). When a tumor grows upward, it can press on the optic nerve and cause the following symptoms.

· Decreased vision: It progresses slowly, so some people do not notice it.

· Visual field defect: Both sides of the visual field look as if covered by a curtain.



If the tumor grows larger, additional symptoms can appear.

· Decreased consciousness: Occurs when the tumor presses on the hypothalamus.

· Hydrocephalus: A condition in which fluid builds up inside the brain. It is rare, but it can be life-threatening.

· Diplopia (double vision): Occurs when the tumor grows sideways and presses on the nerves that move the eye.

· Hypopituitarism: A condition in which the normal pituitary gland is compressed and hormone secretion decreases.



Functioning adenomas cause different symptoms depending on the type of hormone they secrete.

· Prolactin-secreting adenoma: Milk production when not pregnant, menstrual irregularity, and, in severe cases, amenorrhea (absence of menstrual periods) occur.

· Growth hormone-secreting adenoma: Acromegaly, in which the jaw, hands, feet, and other parts become enlarged, occurs.

· ACTH-secreting adenoma: Excess steroid hormones are produced in the body, which can cause Cushing's syndrome, with abdominal obesity, a rounded face, and thinning of the arms and legs.



If you have symptoms like these, please consult a medical specialist.

sections.heading: Diagnosis
sections.content:
If a pituitary tumor is suspected, the following tests are performed.

· MRI: The most important test, which directly shows the location and size of the tumor.

· Visual acuity and visual field tests: Check whether the optic nerve is compressed.

· Hormone tests: Blood tests check which hormone is being secreted in excess.

Please discuss the exact testing plan with your doctor.

sections.heading: Treatment
sections.content:
There are three main approaches to treating a pituitary tumor.



■ Observation

When the tumor is a nonfunctioning adenoma that is small and does not press on surrounding structures, it can be watched with an MRI once a year.



■ Surgery

Surgery is performed when the tumor is a functioning adenoma or is large enough to compress surrounding structures. There are two surgical approaches.

· Endoscopic transsphenoidal surgery: An endoscope is inserted through the nose to remove the tumor. No skin incision is made, and it is easier to tell the normal pituitary gland from the tumor. The hospital stay after surgery is short, 3 to 5 days, so return to daily life can be quick.

· Transcranial approach: Surgery performed by opening the skull, with a hospital stay of about 10 days. It is chosen in special cases.



■ Drug Treatment

Prolactin-secreting adenomas often respond well to drug treatment (dopamine agonists), so it is considered first.



■ Radiation Therapy

When complete removal is difficult because the tumor is attached to surrounding blood vessels or nerves, radiation therapy after surgery may be considered.



The treatment method is determined by your treating specialist according to the patient's condition and the type of tumor. Please be sure to consult a medical specialist thoroughly.

sections.heading: Postoperative Precautions
sections.content:
After surgery through the nose, please keep the following in mind.

There is a thin membrane between the pituitary tumor and the brain. After the tumor is removed, cerebrospinal fluid (the fluid that surrounds the brain and spinal cord) can leak out through this membrane. In the past it occurred in about 5 out of 100 people, but with the development of various methods in recent years, its frequency has been decreasing.

When the likelihood of a leak is high, your care team will give you separate instructions after surgery. If this applies to you, you must be careful with the following actions.

· Sneezing

· Bending your head down when washing your hair

· Straining excessively during a bowel movement

· Other actions that raise the pressure inside the head

If you have any questions, please ask your doctor or care team.

records.title: Costochondritis
records.intro: Costochondritis is a condition in which the cartilage that connects the ribs to the breastbone (sternum) becomes inflamed. Chest pain is the main symptom, and because the symptoms can resemble those of pneumothorax or heart disease, an accurate diagnosis is important. If chest pain persists, please consult a medical specialist.
records.tags_raw: costochondritis, thoracic pain, chest pain, ribs, sternum, cartilage, anti-inflammatory drugs, chest ache, pain in the chest, chest tightness, feeling of stuffiness in the chest, shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, labored breathing, feeling of suffocation, dry cough, persistent minor cough, cough that will not stop
keywords: feeling of stuffiness in the chest

sections.heading: Definition and Symptoms
sections.content:
Costochondritis is a condition in which the cartilage between the ribs and the breastbone becomes inflamed. Chest pain is the main symptom, and it can occur on both sides at the same time. It is characterized by a feeling of pressure in the chest and pain that becomes more noticeable when changing position.



Differences from pneumothorax:

Pneumothorax usually causes pain on one side of the chest and is often accompanied by respiratory symptoms such as difficulty breathing and cough, whereas costochondritis can also occur on both sides and is often unrelated to respiratory symptoms. For both conditions, please consult a medical specialist for an accurate diagnosis.

sections.heading: Causes
sections.content: In most cases it occurs without a clear cause. It can occur when the cartilage is damaged or put under pressure by coughing, strenuous exercise, external impact, or similar causes. Rarely, it is caused by infection with bacteria or other organisms.

sections.heading: Treatment
sections.content:
Most cases of costochondritis may improve with appropriate treatment.



■ Drug Treatment

Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (anti-inflammatory pain relievers) or cough suppressants are used.



■ Rest and Stretching

Symptoms can be eased with enough rest and stretching.



■ Nonsurgical Treatment

If symptoms do not improve with drug treatment and rest, the following methods can be tried.

· Prolotherapy: A method intended to strengthen the cartilage by injecting medication such as concentrated glucose into the painful area.

· Extracorporeal shock wave therapy: A method in which acoustic shock waves are applied to the inflamed area, intended to reduce inflammation and help blood circulation.



■ Surgery

When infectious costochondritis does not improve with antibiotic treatment and observation, surgery is performed to remove pus (drainage and irrigation) or, in severe cases, to remove the cartilage.



Most cases may improve within 2 weeks with appropriate treatment, but if chest pain persists, please consult your doctor.

records.title: Multidrug-Resistant Organisms (Antibiotic-Resistant Bacteria)
records.intro: Multidrug-resistant organisms are bacteria that have developed resistance to several types of antibiotics. They are also called 'superbugs.' Misuse and overuse of antibiotics are the main cause, and infection with them can be very hard to treat. Please take antibiotics only as prescribed by a doctor and for the prescribed length of time. If you have questions about antibiotic use, please consult your doctor.
records.tags_raw: multidrug-resistant organisms, antibiotic resistance, superbug, MRSA, CRE, antibiotic misuse

sections.heading: Prevention and Precautions
sections.content:
To prevent multidrug-resistant organisms, using antibiotics correctly is most important.

· Take all of the antibiotics your doctor prescribed for the full prescribed period. If you stop on your own because your symptoms have improved, the bacteria may not be completely killed and resistant bacteria can develop.
· Do not start or stop antibiotics on your own.
· Do not buy or take antibiotics without a prescription.
· If you have ever had an antibiotic allergy or side effects, be sure to tell your doctor.

sections.heading: Definition
sections.content:
Multidrug-resistant organisms are bacteria that are resistant to several types of antibiotics at the same time. Resistance is the property of bacteria that survive rather than being killed by antibiotics. They are commonly called 'superbugs.'

The main multidrug-resistant organisms include the following.
· MRSA (methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus)
· VRE (vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus)
· CRE (carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales)
· Multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa
· Multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii

sections.heading: Causes
sections.content:
The biggest reason multidrug-resistant organisms develop is misuse and overuse of antibiotics.

Bacteria mutate (change) by themselves in order to survive antibiotics. The more antibiotics are used, the more only resistant bacteria survive and non-resistant bacteria die off. As a result, multidrug-resistant organisms increase.

In particular, using antibiotics when they are not needed, such as for a cold caused by a virus rather than bacteria, is a problem. Most colds are caused by viruses, so antibiotics are not effective.

sections.heading: Risks
sections.content:
When a person is infected with a multidrug-resistant organism, ordinary antibiotics may not work, and the appropriate window for treatment can be missed. In serious infections such as sepsis (a critical condition in which bacteria spread through the blood), it can be life-threatening.

Patients who are hospitalized often receive antibiotics, so they have a higher risk of carrying multidrug-resistant organisms. Medical staff manage them carefully to keep these organisms from spreading to other patients.

records.title: Diabetic Foot (Diabetic Foot Ulcer)
records.intro: Diabetic foot (diabetic foot ulcer) is a complication of diabetes in which an ulcer (sore) forms on the foot and does not heal well. If it is not detected early and treated appropriately, amputation of the foot or leg may become necessary. If you have diabetes, check your feet often, and do not leave even a small wound unattended; please consult a medical specialist.
records.tags_raw: diabetic foot, diabetic foot ulcer, diabetic complications, lower limb reconstruction, amputation, blood vessels, neuropathy

sections.heading: Treatment
sections.content:
Treatment of diabetic foot requires multidisciplinary care in which specialists from several departments work together.

· Blood sugar control: Blood sugar is managed appropriately by endocrinology and metabolism.
· Vascular treatment: Procedures to open or bypass blocked blood vessels are performed.
· Infection treatment: Appropriate antibiotic treatment is given by infectious diseases.
· Reconstructive surgery: Plastic surgery and orthopedics surgically remove infected tissue and restore the defect.

Reconstructive surgery includes skin grafting (a simpler method) and flap surgery (a more complex method). Flap surgery is needed when bone, ligaments, or similar structures are exposed. The treatment method is determined by your treating specialist.

Smoking worsens both diabetes and vascular disease, so you must quit smoking. If you have symptoms (leg pain when walking, or feet that feel cold to the touch), peripheral vascular disease should be suspected and you should seek medical attention immediately.

sections.heading: Prevention
sections.content:
About 10% of people with diabetes develop a foot ulcer, and about 5% of these lead to amputation. Prevention is most important.

· Examine your feet carefully every day: Check the tops and soles of your feet and between your toes for blisters, red areas, and bruises.
· Wash your feet in lukewarm water every day and apply moisturizer. Avoid hot water, electric blankets, and heaters, because they carry a risk of burns.
· Smooth the edges of your toenails to help prevent ingrown toenails.
· Protect your feet by wearing socks and slippers even indoors. Do not walk barefoot.
· Use shoes that are not tight and cushioned insoles.
· Seek immediate medical attention even for a small wound.

After reconstruction is performed successfully, it is important to return quickly to daily life and light exercise. If you become psychologically withdrawn after surgery and move less, it is actually not good for recovery of health.

sections.heading: The Importance of Saving the Foot
sections.content:
There are reports that survival rates drop significantly after leg amputation. On the other hand, when the foot is saved through reconstructive surgery, walking independently may become possible, and keeping up activity can also help with blood sugar control.

When walking becomes difficult, activity decreases and blood sugar control becomes harder, which can worsen overall health. Therefore, active treatment to save the foot is important.

With advances in reconstructive surgery techniques, success rates have improved and recovery periods have become shorter compared with the past.

sections.heading: Causes
sections.content:
In diabetes, a persistently high blood sugar level damages blood vessels and nerves. Diabetic foot occurs when three factors act together.

■ Peripheral Neuropathy
This is the main cause, present in almost 90% of people with diabetic foot ulcers. At first there is burning or stabbing pain, but the longer the disease lasts, the duller the sensation in the feet becomes. As a result, even when a small wound occurs it is not felt, and the wound grows. The skin also becomes dry and cracked, making it vulnerable to infection.

■ Trauma
Even a small wound is dangerous in a person with diabetes. Poorly fitting shoes, calluses, and ingrown toenails can also easily cause an ulcer.

■ Peripheral Vascular Disease
When the peripheral blood vessels (the small blood vessels at the ends of the feet) narrow or become blocked and blood flow decreases, wounds do not heal and can lead to necrosis (tissue death).

records.title: Radiation Therapy
records.intro: Radiation therapy is a treatment that uses high-energy radiation to destroy cancer cells. To help reduce side effects and improve the effect of treatment, it is essential to consult a radiation oncology specialist and to keep up consistent hospital visits.
records.tags_raw: radiation therapy, cancer treatment, X-ray, breast cancer, radiation oncology, lack of energy, listlessness, persistent tiredness

sections.heading: Definition
sections.content: Radiation therapy is a treatment method that delivers X-rays, an invisible form of strong energy, to destroy and kill cancer cells so that they can no longer grow.

sections.heading: How It Works
sections.content: Radiation damages both cancer cells and normal cells. However, normal cells have a greater ability to repair themselves. For this reason, the dose is not given all at once at a high strength; instead, treatment is divided into multiple sessions, giving normal cells time to recover.

sections.heading: Treatment
sections.content: Depending on the type and condition of the cancer, treatment is given in divided daily sessions, from as few as 10 to more than 30. Each session is short and painless, and in recent years, thanks to advanced machines and technology, treatment may even be possible comfortably while clothed, without drawing marks on the body.

sections.heading: Precautions
sections.content: The X-rays used for treatment pass through the body and disappear, so it is safe to be around family members. The most important thing is to go to the hospital on the scheduled days without missing any. If treatment is interrupted, the surviving cancer cells can multiply rapidly again in order to survive.

records.title: Spine Surgery
records.intro: Spinal conditions cause a variety of symptoms, including neck and back pain, numbness in the arms and legs, and gait disturbance. Typical conditions include herniated disc (disc herniation), spinal stenosis, and spondylolisthesis. Most spinal conditions are not life-threatening, so the principle is to start with conservative treatment such as drug therapy and physical therapy, and whether and when surgery is needed depends on each patient's condition. Please consult a medical specialist for an accurate diagnosis and direction of treatment.
records.tags_raw: spine surgery, disc, spinal stenosis, disc herniation, scoliosis, spondylolisthesis, spinal rehabilitation, osteoporosis, lumbar spine, cervical spine, body swelling, facial swelling, leg swelling, swollen hands and feet, numbness in hands and feet, arm numbness, tingling leg, weakness in the arms or legs, difficulty moving one side of the body
keywords: weakness in the arms or legs
difficulty moving one side of the body

sections.heading: When Spine Surgery Is Needed and the Appropriate Timing
sections.content:
■ Treatment Steps

① Conservative treatment such as drug therapy and physical therapy is given first.

② If symptoms do not improve, invasive treatment (treatment in which instruments or medication are placed directly into the body), such as a nerve block (a procedure that reduces inflammation around a nerve with an injection), is given.

③ If, despite these treatments, severe pain that disturbs sleep continues or basic daily activities are difficult, surgery is considered.



■ When Surgery Should Be Done Promptly

When nerve damage (a neurological deficit) such as paralysis of the arms or legs has appeared, surgery becomes the first-line treatment. If the spinal cord (the important bundle of nerves connected to the brain) is compressed, recovery can become difficult.



■ Age and Surgery

Being older does not make surgery itself impossible. Simple disc surgery does not significantly disturb the spinal structures, so it can be performed even in older age. However, with age, osteoporosis (a condition in which the bones weaken) becomes more severe, so in screw fixation surgery the risk of complications such as screws loosening or bones failing to fuse well increases. Recovery can be slower because of reduced muscle mass and general aging, and the risk of general anesthesia is also relatively higher. If the pain is at a tolerable level, conservative treatment is recommended first.

sections.heading: Herniated Disc (Disc Herniation) and Spinal Stenosis
sections.content:
■ Herniated Disc (Disc Herniation)

This is a condition in which the intervertebral disc (the cartilage that acts as a cushion between the vertebrae) is damaged and its inner material is pushed out and presses on a nerve. Over time, the protruding piece of disc can shrink on its own in some cases. According to textbooks it takes about 3 years, but in some patients it improves in as little as 5 to 6 months. Exercise does not heal the disc itself, but if pain is controlled and there is no paralysis, waiting for symptoms to improve while continuing daily life and exercise is also an option.



■ Possibility of Recurrence

Because lumbar (lower back) disc surgery is approached from the back (posterior approach), the problematic piece of disc can be removed sufficiently, but it is difficult to remove completely the damaged tissue that remains inside. For this reason, a possibility of recurrence remains. Cervical (neck) disc surgery is approached from the front and removes the problematic segment almost completely, so recurrence at the same level is uncommon.



■ Spinal Stenosis

The spinal canal is the passage through which the spinal nerves run. Spinal stenosis is a condition in which the bone, ligament, and cartilage tissues that form this passage thicken, narrowing the openings for the nerves and pressing on them. Because stenosis results from thickening (hypertrophy) of tissue, unlike a herniated disc it does not improve on its own and tends to worsen slowly. The fundamental treatment is surgery, but if symptoms are mild or do not greatly interfere with daily life, the condition can be monitored with conservative treatment and exercise.

sections.heading: Recovery After Surgery and Return to Daily Life
sections.content:
If there are no particular complications and there was no nerve damage such as paralysis before surgery, the following course of recovery can be expected. It may differ depending on each patient's condition.



- 2 to 3 days after surgery: The drainage tube and urinary catheter are removed, and walking short distances begins

- 2 weeks after surgery: Basic daily activities such as personal hygiene, eating, and light walking are possible

- 1 month after surgery: Most people can return to work, even after fusion surgery (a major operation that fixes bones with screws)

- 6 months after surgery: High-intensity exercise such as weight training can be started



■ Resuming Exercise

It is best to start exercising with light walking. To let the surgical site stabilize, avoid excessive exercise in the early period.



■ Driving

It is recommended to refrain from driving for about 1 month after surgery, because reaction speed can be reduced during recovery and there is a risk of accidents. If there was no paralysis or other abnormality before or after surgery, driving may be possible right after discharge, but please follow your doctor's instructions.

sections.heading: Leg Swelling After Surgery
sections.content:
The legs sometimes swell right after spine surgery, but spine surgery itself (manipulation of the nerves) is not directly related to leg swelling.



■ Main Causes of Leg Swelling

- Intravenous fluids during surgery: A large amount of saline is given during general anesthesia, and while lying face down for a long time, swelling can develop right after surgery.

- Reduced activity during the rest period: As time spent lying down increases after surgery, leg muscle activity decreases and blood circulation is not smooth, which can cause swelling.

- Lymphatic vessel injury: In surgery approached from the abdominal side (anterior approach), swelling can rarely occur because of injury to lymphatic vessels.



■ Ways to Relieve Swelling

- Wear compression stockings

- Keep the legs raised above the level of the heart

- Start walking as soon as possible



If the swelling is severe or lasts a long time, please tell your doctor.

sections.heading: Everyday Facts About Spine Health
sections.content:
■ If the Spine Curves Sideways, Does a Person Get Shorter?

When the spine is viewed from the front, a sideways curve is called 'scoliosis.' If the spine curves sideways during growth, a person can become shorter and the trunk can bend forward. A normal spine looks straight when viewed from the front, and when viewed from the side it keeps an 'S' shape, in which the cervical spine (neck) and lumbar spine (lower back) curve backward (lordosis) and the thoracic spine (upper back) curves forward (kyphosis).



■ Is a Hard Bed Better?

An excessively hard bed (such as a stone slab bed) can make it difficult to maintain the normal curves of the spine. To maintain the normal curves of the spine, the lower back needs to be able to sink in slightly, but on a hard surface the lower back is pressed flat. An excessively soft bed is also not good, and a bed with slight firmness that can maintain the normal curves of the spine is recommended. Above all, it is important that you feel comfortable.

records.title: Breast Cancer Surgery and Breast Reconstruction
records.intro: Breast cancer is a common cancer in women. Surgical techniques have advanced considerably, making both treatment and reconstruction of the shape of the breast possible. Please do not try to judge a condition from encyclopedia information; be sure to consult a surgery specialist for an examination.
records.tags_raw: breast cancer, breast reconstruction, robotic surgery, breast implant, surgery

sections.heading: Precautions and Regular Checkups
sections.content: Having breast implants does not make you more likely to develop breast cancer. If your health checkup result says 'judgment deferred,' it does not mean everything is fine, so you should visit a hospital right away and have detailed tests.

sections.heading: The Breast Cancer Surgery Process
sections.content: The cancerous lump in the breast is removed, and the lymph nodes in the armpit are checked for spread of the cancer and removed. In recent years, armpit surgery is kept as limited as possible to help prevent the side effect of marked arm swelling (lymphedema).

sections.heading: Robotic Surgery with Less Scarring
sections.content: For early-stage breast cancer, surgery may be performed with a robot through small incisions made only at the armpit or the side of the chest. The scar tends to be hard to see.

sections.heading: Recovery and Skin Sensation
sections.content: About 3 weeks after surgery, people can usually use their arms and shoulders and carry on daily life. Skin sensation at the surgical site becomes dull but usually returns over 1 to 2 years, and even when the breast is reconstructed using abdominal tissue, the effect on later pregnancy and childbirth is generally limited.

sections.heading: Breast Reconstruction Methods
sections.content: The breast left empty after the cancer is removed can be refilled by moving tissue from your own abdomen or back, or by placing an artificial implant, to rebuild a shape that looks natural and similar to the original.

records.title: Robotic Surgery for Gastric Cancer
records.intro: Robotic surgery for gastric cancer is a minimally invasive operation in which a surgeon controls a robot to treat gastric cancer. 'Minimally invasive' refers to a method of operating through only small openings in the body. The surgical method (open, laparoscopic, or robotic) is decided by your treating specialist after considering society guidelines, the latest research findings, and the patient's condition together. Please discuss the most suitable surgical method thoroughly with your treating specialist.
records.tags_raw: gastric cancer, robotic surgery, gastrectomy, laparoscopy, minimally invasive surgery, gastric cancer surgery, chemotherapy, gastric cancer stage, hand tremor, body tremor

sections.heading: Types of Gastric Cancer Surgery
sections.content:
Gastric cancer surgery is broadly divided into three methods.



· Open surgery: Performed by making a direct incision in the abdomen. Because the incision is wide, recovery takes longer and a scar may remain.



· Laparoscopic surgery: A minimally invasive operation performed by making several small openings in the abdomen and inserting a camera and instruments.



· Robotic surgery: A minimally invasive operation in which the surgeon sits at a console (control station) and directly controls the robot. The robot does not move on its own, and the operating surgeon is in charge of the entire operation.



Which method is suitable is judged by your treating specialist according to the location, size, and extent of the tumor and the patient's condition.

sections.heading: Who Robotic Surgery Applies To
sections.content:
Except for early gastric cancer that is currently treated with endoscopic resection, robotic surgery can be considered for gastric cancer of any stage that can be removed surgically.



However, when gastric cancer has spread (metastasized) to other organs, chemotherapy is considered before surgery. Chemotherapy is a treatment that uses drugs to suppress or eliminate the growth of cancer cells.



In addition, the extent of stomach resection is determined not by the surgical method (open, laparoscopic, or robotic) but by the depth of the tumor, how far it has invaded, and whether it has spread. The extent of stomach resection does not change just because the surgery is robotic.



Please discuss whether surgery is possible and which method to use with your treating specialist.

sections.heading: Advantages and Limitations of Robotic Surgery
sections.content:
■ Advantages Compared with Open Surgery

· The incision is smaller, so there tends to be less pain and scarring.

· Recovery is shorter, so return to daily life tends to be quicker.

· The risk of complications may be lower.



■ Characteristics Compared with Laparoscopic Surgery

· The surgical site can be viewed in a 3D image magnified 10 times or more, giving a wider field of view.

· The robotic arms bend like a human wrist, allowing access to deeper areas than laparoscopic instruments.

· The system compensates for the surgeon's hand tremor, allowing precise manipulation.



Some studies report that, compared with laparoscopic surgery, there may be fewer complications and possible oncologic advantages. However, more research is needed before this can be generalized.



■ Limitations

· It is not covered by National Health Insurance, so there is a cost burden.

· Extra preparation time is needed to connect the robot to the patient, so the operation may take 1 to 2 hours longer than open or laparoscopic surgery.

sections.heading: Care Before and After Surgery
sections.content:
Preparation before robotic gastric cancer surgery and care after surgery are similar to those for ordinary gastric cancer surgery (open or laparoscopic).



However, the operation can take longer than with other methods, so the resulting strain on the body must be considered.



Scarring and pain after surgery are similar to those of laparoscopic surgery.



For specifics such as the length of the hospital stay, dietary changes, wound care, and outpatient schedule, please follow the instructions of your care team.

records.title: Robotic Surgery for Hernia
records.intro: A hernia is a condition in which an internal organ moves out of its normal position and pushes out through a weak spot in the abdominal wall. The basic treatment for hernia is surgery, and surgical methods include open surgery, laparoscopic surgery, and robotic surgery. A hernia can recur even after surgery, so ongoing management by your treating specialist is needed regardless of the surgical method. Please discuss the choice of surgical method thoroughly with your treating specialist before deciding.
records.tags_raw: hernia, abdominal wall hernia, inguinal hernia, robotic surgery, laparoscopy, minimally invasive surgery, single-port, recurrence, hand tremor, body tremor

sections.heading: Types of Hernia Surgery
sections.content:
Hernia surgery is broadly divided into three methods.



· Open surgery: Performed by making a direct incision in the abdomen. Because the incision is wide, recovery takes longer and a scar may remain.



· Laparoscopic surgery: A minimally invasive operation performed by making several small openings in the abdomen. 'Minimally invasive' refers to a method of operating with only minimal incisions in the body. It is covered by National Health Insurance, so the cost burden is smaller, but the surgery is technically demanding.



· Robotic surgery: A minimally invasive operation in which the surgeon controls a robot. It uses magnified 3D images and precise robotic arms.



The suitable surgical method is judged by your treating specialist according to the type of hernia and the patient's condition.

sections.heading: What Is Robotic Hernia Surgery?
sections.content:
Robotic surgery is not an operation in which the robot moves on its own. The operating surgeon sits at a console (control station), directly controls the robot, and carries out the entire operation.



· The surgical site can be viewed in a 3D image magnified 10 times or more, which makes precise surgery possible.

· The joints of the robotic arms allow delicate manipulation from a variety of angles.

· The system compensates for the surgeon's hand tremor, creating a stable surgical environment.



For inguinal (groin) hernia, surgery is sometimes done through a single port (a single opening in the navel area). 'Single-port' is a method of operating through only one small opening. However, the surgical approach may differ depending on the type and condition of the hernia.

sections.heading: Advantages and Limitations of Robotic Surgery
sections.content:
■ Advantages

· A wide, precise surgical field of view can be obtained, which helps make surgery safer.

· Precise manipulation is possible even in narrow spaces, which may help reduce the risk of complications.

· In technically demanding cases such as abdominal wall hernia, robotic surgery helps surgeons improve their surgical technique, and its use is gradually increasing.



■ Limitations and Precautions

· The operation can take longer than laparoscopic surgery.

· It is not covered by National Health Insurance, so there may be a cost burden.

· The surgical method differs depending on the patient's condition, so please discuss it thoroughly with your treating specialist.

sections.heading: Preparation Before Surgery
sections.content:
There is no special additional preparation required for robotic hernia surgery. Because the surgery is performed under general anesthesia, the usual preparation before anesthesia, such as fasting, is needed.



The operation can take longer than laparoscopic surgery. It is recommended to leave plenty of time in your schedule on the day of surgery and to be accompanied by a guardian. Please be sure to follow your care team's instructions for specific preparations.

sections.heading: Postoperative Care
sections.content:
Care after surgery, such as the length of the hospital stay, pain management, and wound care, is similar to that for laparoscopic surgery. However, the operation can take longer, so there may be differences during recovery. Please follow your care team's instructions.



A hernia can recur even after surgery. Regardless of the surgical method, if abnormal symptoms appear (such as a bulge, pain, or discomfort at the navel or groin), please consult a medical specialist immediately. It is important to check your recovery through regular outpatient visits.

records.title: Simultaneous Liver-Kidney Transplantation
records.intro: The liver and kidneys have difficulty recovering on their own once they are severely damaged, so transplant surgery may be needed. Because this is a very important, major operation, please consult a transplant specialist thoroughly and receive medical care.
records.tags_raw: liver transplantation, kidney transplantation, organ transplantation, liver cirrhosis, kidney failure

sections.heading: Taking Your Immunosuppressant Medication
sections.content: Take your immunosuppressant medication, which helps your body accept the new organ, every day at the set time without missing a dose. Stopping the medication or reducing the dose on your own may damage the function of the transplanted organs.

sections.heading: Regular Visits to Your Specialist
sections.content: Continuous, careful management is essential even after surgery. Organ function can decline without your noticing, so visit the hospital regularly for blood tests and a thorough check of your condition.

sections.heading: Why the Liver and Kidney Are Transplanted Together
sections.content: In patients with end-stage cirrhosis, kidney function often worsens as well. Receiving a liver and a kidney in a single transplant may help reduce the need for dialysis after surgery and may help improve long-term survival.

sections.heading: Food Safety and Infection Prevention
sections.content: After surgery, you take medication that lowers the body's defenses, so you can be infected more easily by bacteria and viruses. Avoid uncooked raw foods, wash your hands often, and wear a mask when you go out.

sections.heading: Key Precautions After Surgery
sections.content: Smoking or drinking alcohol after a transplant can damage the transplanted organs and increases the risk of cancer and vascular disease. Smoking cessation and alcohol abstinence should be maintained for life.

records.title: Robotic Hepatobiliary and Pancreatic Surgery
records.intro: Robotic surgery is a method in which the surgeon sits at a console (control device) and operates by controlling robotic arms. Using 10x magnified three-dimensional (3D) images and freely moving robotic arms, it can allow more precise manipulation than laparoscopic surgery. It is also used for liver, bile duct, and pancreatic surgery, and for liver donation surgery. Whether robotic surgery is suitable, and which method is used, depends on each patient's condition, so please consult a medical specialist.
records.tags_raw: robotic surgery, laparoscopic surgery, hepatobiliary and pancreatic surgery, liver donation, minimally invasive surgery, living donor liver transplantation, surgical scar, open surgery, lack of energy, lethargy, persistent fatigue

sections.heading: Advantages of Robotic Surgery
sections.content:
■ Surgical Stability

- Reduced fatigue: In conventional laparoscopic surgery, the surgeon had to stand and manipulate instruments for long periods, which could cause reduced concentration and physical fatigue. In robotic surgery, the surgeon sits at a console in a comfortable position, so the operation can be performed steadily even during long procedures.

- Precise view: 10x magnified 3D images allow the surgical site to be seen in much greater detail than in open surgery.

- Free movement: The robotic arms move at various angles, which makes surgery deep inside the body easier and can help preserve major blood vessels and nerves more safely.



■ Advantages for Patients

- Smaller skin incisions may result in smaller scars.

- Pain after surgery may be less, and the hospital stay may be shorter.

- Recovery may be faster.

sections.heading: Cost of Robotic Surgery
sections.content:
Robotic surgery is expensive because the consumable supplies that must be replaced for each operation (such as disposable instruments at the tips of the robotic arms) are costly. Rather than the surgical fee itself, the cost of consumables accounts for a substantial portion of the total cost. Some private indemnity health insurance plans currently cover the cost of robotic surgery.



The cost of robotic surgery and insurance coverage vary by hospital and type of surgery, so please check with the hospital in advance.

sections.heading: Robotic Surgery for Liver Donation
sections.content:
Robotic surgery is also used for liver donation (surgery in which a healthy person donates part of the liver for living donor liver transplantation).



■ Scar Comparison

- Conventional open surgery: A long J-shaped scar remains on the abdomen.

- Robotic/laparoscopic surgery: Only five small openings for the surgical instruments and an incision of about 13 cm, through which the donated liver is removed, remain. This incision is located below the underwear line, so it is not visible in everyday life.



■ Operating Time and Outcomes

The amount of bleeding during surgery and whether blood vessels or bile ducts are injured affect outcomes more than operating time does. With 10x magnified images, robotic surgery can help preserve blood vessels and bile ducts more safely.



■ When Robotic Surgery Is Not Possible

There are few cases in which robotic surgery cannot be performed because of the surgical method itself. However, donation itself may be difficult if the donor's liver is not suitable for the recipient or if the amount of liver remaining after donation would be too small.

sections.heading: Robotic/Laparoscopic Pancreaticoduodenectomy (Whipple Procedure) and Pancreatectomy
sections.content:
Pancreatectomy is performed for various pancreatic diseases, including pancreatic cancer, pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors, and intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasm (IPMN). Depending on the location of the tumor, pancreaticoduodenectomy, which removes the head of the pancreas, or distal pancreatectomy, which removes the body and tail of the pancreas, may be performed. Robotic/laparoscopic surgery may be used depending on the patient's condition and the extent of the disease.



■ Surgical Procedure



- Conventional open surgery: An incision is made in the abdomen, and the diseased part of the pancreas and the surrounding lymph nodes are removed.



- Robotic/laparoscopic surgery: Small openings are made in the abdomen, and robotic or laparoscopic instruments are inserted to perform the surgery. Removal and suturing are performed using magnified 3D images and precise robotic instruments.



■ Features of Robotic/Laparoscopic Surgery



The pancreas is close to major blood vessels, the bile duct, and the gastrointestinal tract, so delicate surgery is required. Robotic/laparoscopic surgery allows careful dissection and suturing while viewing narrow, deep areas under magnification, so some patients may benefit in terms of wounds, pain, and recovery.



■ Criteria for Robotic/Laparoscopic Pancreaticoduodenectomy and Pancreatectomy



Open surgery may be more appropriate if the cancer has extensively invaded major blood vessels, if there is severe inflammation or adhesions, or if the patient's overall condition is poor. The surgical method is chosen with safety and complete removal of the cancer as the top priorities.

sections.heading: Limitations on the Use of Robotic Surgery
sections.content:
Robotic surgery is not suitable for every patient. In the following cases, open surgery or another approach may be more appropriate.



- When there are severe adhesions from previous surgery (organs stuck together)

- When the cancer is located very close to major blood vessels

- When the patient's overall condition makes it difficult to tolerate a long operation



Please decide on the surgical method after thorough consultation with your doctor, based on a comprehensive review of imaging results and your overall condition.

sections.heading: Preparation and Recovery Before and After Surgery
sections.content:
Preparation and recovery before and after robotic surgery are similar to those for conventional surgery.



■ Before Surgery

- Blood tests, imaging tests, and other examinations are used to confirm whether surgery is possible.

- Be sure to tell your doctor before surgery about any medications you are taking (especially those that affect blood clotting).



■ After Surgery

- Pain is often less and the hospital stay is often shorter than with open surgery.

- Recovery instructions, such as dietary and activity restrictions, may differ depending on the surgical site, so follow the guidance of your healthcare team.



※ The information in this Health Encyclopedia is for reference purposes only. For accurate diagnosis and treatment, please consult a medical specialist.

records.title: Robotic Surgery for Liver Cancer and Liver Transplantation
records.intro: Robotic surgery is a method in which the surgeon controls a robot and operates through a few small openings in the abdomen. A more expensive operation is not always the better choice. Do not decide based on this encyclopedia alone; please consult a surgical specialist to find the safest surgical method for the patient.
records.tags_raw: liver cancer, liver transplantation, robotic surgery, general surgery, liver cirrhosis

sections.heading: Dietary Precautions After Surgery
sections.content: After part of the liver has been removed, liver function is markedly reduced, so do not drink alcohol or smoke until you have recovered. Taking unverified products believed to be good for health, such as tree-bark decoctions, herbal medicines, or extracts, without medical advice may damage even the remaining liver, so great caution is needed.

sections.heading: Surgical Outcomes and Safety
sections.content: A somewhat longer preparation time for surgery does not necessarily have a negative effect on the patient. Because the surgeon can view the surgical site enlarged and control bleeding carefully to reduce blood loss, the operation itself may be performed more safely.

sections.heading: Characteristics of Robotic Surgery for Liver Donors
